items.title: Immersion patriotique : Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo appelle les jeunes à être « les fers de lance de la transformation » du Burkina
items.description: Le ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, a effectué, ce vendredi 7 août 2026, une visite d’encouragement sur le site du Lycée Wend-Pouiré de Saaba, où sont logés les appelés de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) 2026. Cette sortie visait à manifester le soutien du Gouvernement aux jeunes engagés dans ce programme de renforcement du civisme, du patriotisme et de l’esprit de service à la Nation. Le ministre était accompagné de la ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, du gouverneur de la région du Kadiogo, ainsi que des autorités communales, religieuses, coutumières et militaires. La deuxième édition de l’IPO, destinée à cultiver l’amour de la patrie chez les jeunes bacheliers burkinabè, bat son plein sur l’ensemble du territoire. Un aperçu des immergés à Saaba Dans la région du Kadiogo, 44 sites accueillent les appelés. Au lycée Wend-Pouiré de Saaba, ce sont 699 jeunes qui suivent actuellement le programme. C’est pour témoigner sa proximité avec ces acteurs que le Gouvernement, par la voix du ministre de l'Économie et des Finances, est venu les rencontrer. À cette occasion, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo a adressé ses encouragements aux nouveaux bacheliers, saluant à la fois leur réussite au Baccalauréat et leur engagement dans cette initiative. « Je voudrais d’abord et avant tout vous féliciter pour votre brillante réussite, mais également pour votre implication dans l’immersion patriotique », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que cette expérience constitue une opportunité unique pour la jeunesse burkinabè. Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo invitant les immergés à refléter les valeurs apprises à la fin de l'IPO Le ministre de l'Économie a échangé avec les appelés, les exhortant à faire de cette immersion un véritable cadre d’apprentissage du civisme, de la solidarité et de l’engagement patriotique. Il les a invités à mettre en pratique les valeurs acquises pour contribuer activement à la transformation du Burkina Faso. Selon Dr Nacanabo, l’IPO va bien au-delà des connaissances théoriques : elle permet d’apprendre le vivre-ensemble, la discipline et le sens du service public. « Vous venez d’horizons divers et vous apprenez à vivre ensemble. Cela, c’est la solidarité », a-t-il souligné. Le ministre Aboubakar Nacanabo a, par ailleurs, insisté sur le rôle déterminant de la jeunesse dans l’avenir du pays. Citant une adresse du Président du Faso aux chercheurs et universitaires, il a rappelé que « le Burkina Faso a besoin de citoyens qui ont un cerveau plein de connaissances, mais surtout un cœur plein de patriotisme ». Dans cette dynamique, le ministre de l'Économie a appelé les jeunes à devenir des acteurs majeurs de la transformation nationale. « Vous êtes les fers de lance de cette transformation », a-t-il affirmé, en rappelant que la Révolution progressiste populaire repose sur une rupture avec certaines pratiques pour construire un Burkina Faso meilleur. Emmanuel Bénaja Yempabou Tendano, expliquant le quotidien des appelés Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo a également invité les participants à ne pas limiter les enseignements de l’immersion à la seule durée du camp. Il leur a demandé de traduire les valeurs acquises dans leur comportement quotidien, afin que leur passage par l’IPO se reflète durablement dans leurs actes. Il les a encouragés à tirer pleinement profit de la formation en restant attentifs aux enseignements de leurs formateurs. « Faites en sorte que chaque minute passée ici soit une minute de qualité, une minute d’apprentissage », a-t-il recommandé. Interrogé sur le rythme de vie au camp, l’appelé Emmanuel Bénaja Yempabou Tendano, de la 1re compagnie, 6e section de l’IPO 2026, a confié que les premiers jours d’adaptation avaient été un peu difficiles, avant que lui et ses camarades ne s’habituent progressivement à la cadence. Il a décrit une journée type qui débute à 5 heures par le rassemblement, le contrôle des effectifs et les activités sportives, suivis de la montée des couleurs. Les appelés enchaînent ensuite avec les cours jusqu’à la mi-journée, puis reprennent les activités pédagogiques l’après-midi. La journée s’achève par la descente des couleurs, les exercices d’ordre serré et de défilé, avant le dîner et le retour aux dortoirs à 20 heures. Évoquant la visite du ministre, Emmanuel Tendano a estimé qu’elle constituait une véritable source de motivation. « Cela nous montre que nous ne travaillons pas pour rien. Les autorités suivent ce que nous apprenons et nous encouragent à poursuivre nos efforts pour assurer, demain, la relève », a-t-il exprimé. Une photo de famille des immergés avec les officiels En clôture de sa visite, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo s’est dit satisfait et a souhaité plein succès aux appelés, tout en indiquant qu’il les retrouverait lors de la cérémonie de clôture pour constater les acquis de leur formation. Outre les échanges avec les immergés, le ministre et sa délégation ont procédé à des plantations d’arbres fruitiers et ont visité l’infirmerie, la cuisine ainsi que les dortoirs du site. Lire aussi : Burkina : Immersion patriotique obligatoire pour les élèves Jean-François SOMÉ Minute.bf

items.title: Bilawal claims 'certain elements' within PML-N are sowing division among allies, undermining PM Shehbaz
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari claimed on Friday that certain elements within the ruling PML-N were undermining Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and sowing discord between him and his political allies. The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases. The PPP chief was addressing an election rally in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s Poonch district, where the third phase of elections in the region is slated to be held. “High-profile people are saying that the government has collapsed. I’m not saying that, nor am I casting doubt on the prime minister’s intentions. He’s a good man with good intentions. But what can he do when the people around him have bad intentions?” Bilawal asked. In reference to remarks he made earlier this week, the party chief highlighted that the PPP did not start the “countdown” to the government’s collapse, but rather these elements within the ruling party. “The PML-N’s fight is not with the PPP — it happens in elections, as it has before. The real fight is entirely different, because the PM, with his good intentions and actions, is undermined by a large part of the PML-N,” Bilawal alleged. “A big part of the PML-N wants the PM to fight not only the opposition, but also his own allies.” He then asked the audience: “Have there ever been elections held in six phases in Kashmir’s history? If Kashmir is one, then the election should have been held on a single day.” Bilawal said the elections were being held in phases “so that there is calm and the elections are peaceful, free and fair”, before asking: “But in which phase were the elections free, fair or peaceful?” “In truth, elections were carried out in phases so they could rig them. They knew that 10 seats were in their pocket from the start,” he alleged. “With the 10 seats in their pocket, they robbed Mirpur, they robbed Muzaffarabad, and they’re looking at you, in Poonch. They are looking at Bagh. On August 10, they will find out that those in Poonch and Bagh hunt tigers.” Elections are being held across AJK in three phases . Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively. The first phase of polling in Mirpur saw the PML-N secure nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four. In the second phase in Muzaffarabad, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally. The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district. However, earlier today, the AJK Election Commission revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation. The electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri would not be held on August 10, the Election Commission said, adding that it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch. It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”. The commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June , with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically. The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. The government has accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest.

items.title: Le PSV rejette une offre des Rangers pour Couhaib Driouech
items.description: L'avenir de Couhaib Driouech continue d'alimenter les rumeurs du mercato. Selon les informations de Foot Mercato, le PSV Eindhoven a refusé une première offre des Rangers, qui souhaitaient recruter l'ailier marocain. Le club écossais avait proposé 7 millions d'euros pour s'attacher les services de l'international marocain U23. Une offre jugée insuffisante par les dirigeants du PSV, qui ne comptent pas brader leur joueur. Malgré ce premier refus, le dossier reste ouvert. Toujours selon la même source, Burnley et le Celta Vigo suivent également de près la situation de Driouech et ont déjà entamé des discussions en vue d'un éventuel transfert. Un club de Ligue 1, dont le nom n'a pas été dévoilé, surveillerait lui aussi le dossier et étudierait la possibilité de passer à l'action dans les prochaines semaines. Les Rangers, de leur côté, n'ont pas totalement abandonné la piste, même s'ils explorent parallèlement d'autres options pour renforcer leur secteur offensif. Arrivé au PSV Eindhoven en 2024, Couhaib Driouech s'est rapidement imposé comme l'un des éléments offensifs les plus prometteurs du club néerlandais. Le Marocain a disputé 61 rencontres sous le maillot du PSV, inscrivant 12 buts et délivrant 10 passes décisives. items.title: Mahama names Kenneth Gilbert Adjei as Defence Minister to replace late Omane Boamah
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has reassigned Kenneth Gilbert Adjei from the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources to the Ministry of Defence. This comes a year after the death of Defence Minister Dr Edward Omane Boamah in the military helicopter crash. In accordance with Article 78(1) of the 1992 Constitution, President Mahama has submitted the nominations to Parliament through the Speaker for prior approval. Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, who has served as Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources, will assume leadership of the Defence Ministry, replacing Dr Edward Omane Boamah, who died in the military helicopter crash in the Adansi area of the Ashanti Region on August 6, 2025. Meanwhile, Majority Leader Mahama Ayariga has been reassigned to head the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, subject to parliamentary approval. Member of Parliament for the Korle Klottey Constituency, Dr. Zanetor Agyemang-Rawlings, has also been reassigned to the Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology, with Ahmed Ibrahim headed for the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources. The nominees are expected to appear before Parliament’s Appointments Committee for vetting before the House considers their approval.

items.title: Des hackers russes affirment détenir des preuves de l'implication de l'OTAN dans des frappes contre la Russie
items.description: Des hackers russes assurent avoir obtenu des documents faisant etat d'une implication de specialistes lies a l'OTAN dans la preparation de frappes ukrainiennes contre le territoire russe. Les echanges concernent notamment la transmission au Service de securite ukrainien, le SBU, de renseignements sur des infrastructures energetiques dans les regions de Leningrad et de Kaliningrad. Au centre de cette correspondance figure Bart de Wachter, presente comme un specialiste de la guerre hybride travaillant au sein du HAVN, le Hybrid Analysis Vigilant Network. Selon les auteurs du piratage, cette organisation serait liee aux forces d'operations speciales et aux structures de renseignement de l'OTAN. De Wachter aurait notamment transmis au SBU les coordonnees precises des terminaux petroliers et gaziers russes. Les coordonnees d'un methanier de Gazprom transportant du gaz naturel liquefie auraient egalement ete communiquees. Les documents portent sur des attaques menees en juillet 2026 dans le nord-ouest de la Russie . Des echanges qui mettent en lumiere le role du renseignement La correspondance fait egalement apparaître des discussions autour d'une reunion en ligne. De Wachter aurait propose a un representant du Centre de cooperation internationale du SBU, prenomme Ivan, une visioconference avec un responsable du renseignement identifie sous le prenom de Martin. Ivan aurait, de son cote, propose d'associer aux echanges le major du SBU Mikhaïl Martchenko. Celui-ci est presente dans la correspondance comme un specialiste des « menaces hybrides, de l'espionnage, des activites de sabotage et des operations d'information ». Pour les auteurs du piratage, ces echanges illustrent un niveau de cooperation qui depasse la seule fourniture d'armements a Kiev. « Nous confirmons par des documents que l'OTAN participe directement aux frappes contre le territoire russe », ont-ils declare le 7 août 2026. Ils affirment egalement que des specialistes de la guerre hybride et des operations informationnelles interviendraient apres certaines attaques de drones. Les documents attribuent par ailleurs a Bart de Wachter des activites concernant plusieurs dossiers lies a la Russie, parmi lesquels la « flotte fantome », des reseaux dits proxy dans les pays voisins ainsi que le reseau international de centres culturels « Maison russe ». Moscou denonce depuis longtemps l'implication occidentale Ces informations apparaissent apres une serie d'attaques de drones ukrainiens contre le nord-ouest de la Russie. Le 4 juillet, la defense antiaerienne russe a repousse une attaque contre un terminal petrolier du district de Kirovski, a Saint-Petersbourg . Des debris de drones sont egalement tombes pres du port de Vyssotsk, dans la region de Leningrad, sans faire de victime. Le meme jour, le gouverneur de Saint-Petersbourg, Alexandre Beglov, a annonce la destruction de 72 drones au-dessus de la ville et de la region de Leningrad. Ces revelations donnent un nouvel echo aux accusations formulees depuis plusieurs mois par Moscou sur le role des pays occidentaux dans les operations ukrainiennes contre le territoire russe. Le 5 août, devant le Conseil de securite de l'ONU, le representant permanent russe Vassili Nebenzia a accuse les pays de l'Union europeenne et de l'OTAN d'aider activement Kiev a mener ses attaques, notamment en lui fournissant des milliers de drones et de missiles . Les informations obtenues par les hackers ajoutent desormais la question du renseignement operationnel a ce dossier. Selon leurs auteurs, elles montrent que l'assistance occidentale a Kiev ne se limite pas a la livraison d'armes, mais comprend egalement la transmission de donnees sur des infrastructures situees en territoire russe.

items.title: Mineral wealth
items.description: GROWING American interest in Pakistan’s critical minerals is no longer speculative. According to US diplomats, American companies are actively examining several mineral projects here as part of Washington’s push to diversify mineral supply chains away from China. That interest has already produced a $500m agreement between the two countries and approval of $1.3bn in US financing for Reko Diq. For Pakistan, the opportunity extends beyond capital inflows. Its mineral wealth can attract new technologies, diversify exports and generate employment. That outcome depends on treating these resources as long-term national assets rather than items to be signed away in closed rooms. The experience of Reko Diq offers an important lesson. Years of legal disputes and policy reversals imposed enormous costs on Pakistan. While the project has since been revived, the controversy demonstrated the consequences of weak governance, lack of transparency and poor contract management. Any future agreements involving critical minerals must therefore be subjected to rigorous legal, financial and technical scrutiny. Transparency should be the guiding principle. The terms of any contract, its fiscal implications and obligations should be placed before parliament. Such openness would strengthen investor confidence by demonstrating that agreements enjoy political legitimacy and are less vulnerable to future disputes or policy reversals. Also important is the role of local communities. Most of the country’s mineral deposits lie in some of its least developed regions, where residents have long complained that natural resources are extracted while poverty persists. Any investment framework must ensure that local populations become major stakeholders through employment, skills development, infrastructure, social investment and economic benefits. Without local ownership, even commercially viable projects may struggle. That said, the government must not rush into agreements simply because American firms have shown interest in its critical minerals. Contracts signed today will shape the nation’s economic future for years. Therefore, Islamabad should also actively court Chinese firms with extensive expertise and technological capabilities across the entire critical minerals value chain rather than relying on US firms alone. A competition between Chinese and US investors can ultimately work in Pakistan’s favour, attracting better commercial terms, and encouraging higher standards of technology transfer and value addition. Published in Dawn, August 7th, 2026

items.title: Mémorial Thomas-Sankara: 2ème cérémonial militaire au Président Thomas Sankara et à ses 12 compagnons
items.description: Le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO a pris part ce jeudi 6 août 2026, au dixième cérémonial d’hommage militaire au Président Thomas Sankara et à ses douzes compagnons. Il avait à ses côtés, le Ministre de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem PODA, président de l'acte 10 du cérémonial d'hommage militaire. Prenant la parole, le Ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO a rappelé la symbolique du cérémonial qui n'est pas une cérémonie ordinaire mais un hommage au Père de la Révolution d'août 1983, le Président Thomas SANKARA. « Nous voulons que chacun d'entre vous entre en lui-même et mène une introspection sur ce que notre pays doit être parce que Thomas SANKARA a tracé les sillons à travers la Révolution Démocratique et Populaire ». Le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, porte-parole du gouvernement, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo Le Ministre de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem PODA, a salué l'institution de ce cérémonial d'hommage qui est un devoir de mémoire pour demeurer fidèle aux idéaux de patriotisme, d'intégrité, de justice sociale et de souveraineté du Capitaine Noël Isidore Thomas SANKARA. Il a rappelé que c'est sous l'impulsion du Président SANKARA que le premier Code des investissements a été élaboré ainsi que la création du Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Enfin, le Ministre chargé de la Communication a invité la communauté des hommes d'affaires Burkinabè ainsi que les amis du Burkina Faso à investir dans le projet « Ma brique pour SANKARA », estimé à 117 milliards F CFA. A terme, ce projet verra la construction sur le site du Mémorial Thomas SANKARA, en plus du Mausolée, une tour de 87m de hauteur, 14 statues dédiées à Sankara, ses douze compagnons et au Président d'honneur du Mémorial, John Jerry RAWLINGS. Il comprendra également une bibliothèque, un amphithéâtre de 3000 places, une salle polyvalente, un centre commercial, un parcours thématique, un jardin botanique, un espace de repos et de loisirs et un téléphérique. items.title: Nazinon/Reboisement: « Planter un arbre, c’est planter une vie », affirme le directeur régional des mines
items.description: Nazinon/Reboisement: « Planter un arbre, c'est planter une vie », affirme le directeur régional des mines Manga, 6 août 2026 (AIB) – La Direction régionale des mines et des carrières du Nazinon a procédé, jeudi, au reboisement de l'espace vert du secteur 4 de la ville de Manga. A cette occasion, son directeur régional, Hervé Kalmogo, a invité les populations riveraines à protéger et à entretenir les jeunes plants, affirmant que « planter un arbre, c'est planter une vie ». Cette opération de reboisement s'inscrit dans le cadre de l'appel lancé par les plus hautes autorités du Burkina Faso en faveur de la restauration du couvert végétal, à travers l'initiative « Ma concession, mon arbre ». S'adressant aux participants et aux riverains, M. Kalmogo a insisté sur la responsabilité collective dans la préservation des plants mis en terre. « C'est nous qui avons certes planté ces arbres, mais en réalité, c'est vous qui en êtes les bénéficiaires directs », a-t-il déclaré, rappelant le rôle essentiel des arbres dans la lutte contre la dégradation de l'environnement et l'amélioration du cadre de vie des populations. Selon lui, chaque citoyen doit contribuer à la protection du patrimoine forestier, car « planter un arbre, c'est planter une vie ». Intervenant au nom du directeur provincial de l'Environnement et du Cadre de vie du Zoundwéogo, le lieutenant Issouf Ouattara a exhorté les populations à assurer l'entretien et le suivi des jeunes plants, dans l'attente de la mise en place d'un dispositif d'adduction d'eau destiné à faciliter leur arrosage. Il a indiqué que cette activité s'inscrit dans la vision des autorités nationales visant à accélérer la restauration du couvert végétal et à renforcer les actions de protection de l'environnement. L'activité a mobilisé les populations riveraines ainsi que plusieurs services techniques, témoignant d'un engagement collectif en faveur de la préservation de l'environnement. Agence d'information du Burkina SM/BGB/bak

items.title: Canada updates visa processing times for Nigerians as study permit wait rises
items.description: Nigerians applying to study or travel in Canada are facing longer estimated processing times after Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) released its latest temporary residence update. IRCC updated its processing-time estimates on August 5, 2026, with the latest figures showing increases across several temporary residence categories. For Nigerian applicants, the estimated processing time for study permits increased from six weeks to seven weeks between July 28 and August 5. The wait for Canadian visitor visas also increased, rising from 64 days to 68 days. However, the estimated processing time for Nigerians applying for a work permit remained unchanged at seven weeks. There was also a slight increase in the estimated processing time for super visa applications from Nigeria, which rose from 41 days to 43 days. The latest figures mean Nigerian applicants should expect the following estimated waits: Work permit: 7 weeks Study permit: 7 weeks Visitor visa: 68 days Super visa: 43 days The changes in Canada’s latest update were not limited to Nigerian applicants. Work permit processing for applicants from Pakistan recorded one of the biggest increases, jumping from 11 weeks to 25 weeks, a rise of 14 weeks. Study permit processing for applicants from the Philippines also increased by one week, while super visa processing for applicants from the Philippines rose from 73 days to 100 days. Some applicants, however, saw their estimated waiting periods fall. The biggest reduction among the featured categories was recorded for super visa applications from Pakistan, which dropped from 196 days to 185 days. What Nigerians should know IRCC’s processing times are estimates and do not represent a guaranteed date for when an application will be completed. The actual time required to process an application can vary depending on factors such as the complexity of the case, the number of applications awaiting processing, available resources and whether immigration officials require additional information or documents. The Canadian immigration department updates temporary residence processing times weekly, meaning the estimates for Nigerian applicants could change again in the next update. The next update is expected around August 12, 2026. Vanguard News The post Canada updates visa processing times for Nigerians as study permit wait rises appeared first on Vanguard News .

Les participants à l’atelier ont été renseignés sur l’arrêté régissant la fabrication, le montage, l’importation et la distribution de ces engins. Selon une information de la Brigade Mobile de Contrôle Économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF), les acteurs économiques de la filière des cycles, cyclomoteurs et motocycles, ont pris part, le jeudi 6 août 2026, à un atelier d’information et de sensibilisation consacré au nouvel arrêté régissant la fabrication, le montage, l’importation et la distribution de ces engins. L'objectif principal de cet atelier était d'échanger en toute franchise sur les enjeux de la nouvelle réglementation, ses objectifs clés et ses innovations majeures. «Il s'agit de créer les conditions d'un marché transparent, concurrentiel et équilibré, dans lequel le prix payé par le consommateur est réellement justifié par les coûts de mise à disposition du produit», a laissé entendre le Coordonnateur général de la BMCRF, Sanibè Faho. A l’issue de la formation, un calendrier précis de mise en conformité a été dévoilé. Il s’agit du ​25 août 2026 correspondant à la date limite de conformité pour l'ensemble des importateurs et distributeurs. Celle du 25 mai 2027 correspond à la date limite de conformité pour les fabricants et les unités de montage. items.title: Koulsé/Éducation: Les performances aux examens scolaires saluées par le Cadre régional de développement
items.description: Koulsé/Éducation: Les performances aux examens scolaires saluées par le Cadre régional de développement Kaya, 5 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Cadre régional de développement (CRD) des Koulsé, réuni vendredi 5 août 2026 sa deuxième session ordinaire de l'année, a salué les performances enregistrées par la région aux examens scolaires et professionnels de la session 2026, marquées par une nette progression des taux de réussite dans l'ensemble des filières. Au niveau de l'examen du Certificat d'études primaires (CEP) la Région a enregistré 18 001 candidats inscrits, dont 17 481 présents dans 101 centres d'examen répartis en 35 jurys. Le taux de réussite de 96,17 %, est en hausse de quatre points par rapport à la session de 2025 et supérieur à la moyenne nationale. Au Brevet d'études du premier cycle (BEPC), 4 301 candidats ont été admis sur 8 031 présents, soit un taux de réussite de 53,55 %, en progression de 7,45 points. Le Baccalauréat affiche 63,89 % de succès avec 2 222 admis sur 3 478 présents, contre 58,40 % en 2025, soit une hausse de 5,49 points. L'enseignement et la formation techniques et professionnels enregistrent aussi des résultats encourageants avec des taux de réussite de 87,72 % au Certificat d'aptitude professionnelle (CAP), 86,58 % au Brevet d'études professionnelles (BEP), 90,05 % au Certificat de qualification professionnelle (CQP) et 96,23 % au Brevet de qualification professionnelle (BQP), tous en progression par rapport à la session précédente. Selon les responsables en charge de l'éducation, ces performances s'expliquent notamment par le retour progressif des élèves dans les écoles, la réouverture de plusieurs établissements, la qualité de l'encadrement pédagogique ainsi que les efforts conjugués des autorités, des Forces de défense et de sécurité et des partenaires de l'éducation. La secrétaire générale de la région, Bernadette Adenyo/Sermé, président le CRD, a félicité l'ensemble des acteurs du système éducatif pour ces performances obtenues malgré un contexte sécuritaire difficile. Elle les a invités à maintenir cette dynamique afin de consolider les acquis et de poursuivre la quête de l'excellence dans les établissements de la région. Agence d'Information du Burkina AIO/bak

If confirmed, she’ll replace the late Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Murtala Mohammed. The President has also nominated Bawku Central MP Mahama Ayariga as Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, while reassigning two other ministers to new portfolios. The nominations were submitted to Parliament on Friday, August 7, 2026, in accordance with Article 78(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which requires parliamentary approval before ministers can assume office. Dr Zanetor Agyemang-Rawlings, the daughter of former President Jerry John Rawlings and former First Lady Nana Konadu Agyemang-Rawlings, has represented the Klottey Korle constituency in Parliament since 2017. Her appointment comes after months of speculation over her possible elevation to cabinet, with the legislator having served on Parliament’s Environment, Science and Technology Committee and advocated for measures to address environmental challenges, including flooding. The Environment portfolio had remained without a substantive minister following the death of Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed in the August 2025 helicopter crash that also claimed the life of former Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane Boamah. As part of the changes, President Mahama has reassigned Kenneth Gilbert Adjei from the Ministry of Works and Housing to the Ministry of Defence. Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, who had been acting as Defence Minister since the death of Dr Omane Boamah, is expected to hand over the portfolio once the new nominees are approved. The President has also reassigned Ahmed Ibrahim, Member of Parliament for Banda, to the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources. The appointments were announced in a statement signed by Felix Kwakye Ofosu, MP, Spokesperson to the President and Minister for Government Communications. The nominees are expected to appear before Parliament’s Appointments Committee for vetting before their names are submitted to the House for approval. The changes come as President Mahama continues efforts to strengthen his administration and fill positions that became vacant following the August 2025 tragedy that claimed the lives of eight officials, including two cabinet ministers.

items.title: Sécurité des mineurs en ligne: Meta écope d’une sanction financière de 942 millions de dollars
items.description: La justice du Nouveau-Mexique a alourdi, le jeudi 6 août 2026, la sanction financière visant Meta dans le dossier de la protection des enfants sur ses réseaux sociaux. Selon des sources médiatiques, une nouvelle amende de 567 millions de dollars vient s'ajouter à une première condamnation, portant la note totale à 942 millions de dollars pour le géant américain. Le groupe dirigé par Mark Zuckerberg a été frappé jeudi 6 août 2026 d'une lourde sanction financière dans le cadre d'un contentieux relatif à la sécurité des jeunes utilisateurs de ses plateformes. La justice du Nouveau-Mexique a fixé à 567 millions de dollars le montant d'une nouvelle amende, qui vient compléter une précédente pénalité de 375 millions de dollars déjà prononcée dans ce même dossier, portant ainsi la facture globale à 942 millions de dollars. Selon des médias qui citent le juge Bryan Biedscheid, ce dernier a estimé, dans son ordonnance, que le comportement de Meta relevait d'une «nuisance publique», jugeant que les répercussions de ses pratiques dépassaient le seul cadre numérique pour affecter directement les foyers, les écoles et la société dans son ensemble. Cette bataille judiciaire, ouverte en 2023, reprochait à l'entreprise un manque de vigilance face à l'exposition des enfants à des contenus sexuels et à des individus malveillants rôdant sur ses plateformes. Le système de recommandation algorithmique du groupe était lui aussi pointé du doigt. Au terme de la procédure, la justice a retenu plusieurs manquements à la réglementation du Nouveau-Mexique en matière de protection des consommateurs. Propriétaire de Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp et Threads, Meta rejette cette décision et annonce vouloir interjeter appel. Le groupe assure poursuivre ses investissements conséquents dans les outils censés préserver ses jeunes usagers. Outre le volet financier, la justice exige de l'entreprise un renforcement concret de ses dispositifs de protection. Le tribunal réclame notamment un encadrement plus strict des échanges entre adultes et mineurs, la disparition du compteur de «likes» visible pour les utilisateurs de moins de 18 ans, ainsi qu'une restriction des notifications nocturnes. Le temps passé quotidiennement sur Facebook et Instagram par les adolescents devrait, par ailleurs, être plafonné à environ trois heures. Cette nouvelle condamnation intervient alors que Meta reste sous le feu de multiples procédures judiciaires aux États-Unis concernant l'impact de ses plateformes sur la jeunesse, dans un climat international où l'encadrement des réseaux sociaux à destination des mineurs se durcit progressivement. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Sécurité des mineurs en ligne: Meta écope d'une sanction financière de 942 millions de dollars est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Pêche | Les exportateurs tunisiens doivent respecter les normes d’emballage de l’UE
items.description: Les entreprises tunisiennes exportant des produits de la pêche et de l’aquaculture vers l'Union européenne ont été invitées à se conformer d’urgence aux nouvelles normes communautaires en matière d’emballages, qui entreront en vigueur le 12 août 2026. Cet appel a été lancé par la Direction générale des services vétérinaires (DGSV) de Tunisie et relayé par le Groupement interprofessionnel des produits de la pêche (Gipp), qui recommandent aux établissements exportateurs d’engager immédiatement les démarches nécessaires auprès de leurs fournisseurs d’emballages afin de vérifier la conformité des matériaux utilisés au nouveau cadre européen. Le règlement de l’UE 2025/40 relatif aux emballages et aux déchets d’emballages, connu sous l’acronyme PPWR, est entré en vigueur le 11 février 2025 et sera applicable de manière générale à partir du 12 août 2026. La réglementation concerne tous les emballages mis sur le marché européen, quels que soient le matériau et le pays d’origine, et introduit des exigences relatives à la composition, à la durabilité, à la recyclabilité, à l’étiquetage et à la documentation technique. Pour les emballages destinés au contact alimentaire – y compris ceux utilisés pour le poisson frais, congelé, transformé ou conservé – des limitations sont également prévues concernant la présence de substances per- et polyfluoroalkylées (PFAS) au-delà de certains seuils. Les fabricants devront être en mesure de démontrer la conformité des emballages au moyen d’une documentation technique et d’une déclaration UE, tandis que les fournisseurs seront tenus de transmettre les informations nécessaires. Cet avertissement des autorités revêt une importance particulière pour la filière halieutique tunisienne, fortement tournée vers les marchés européens. En 2025, la Tunisie a exporté 35 500 tonnes de produits de la pêche pour une valeur de 878 millions de dinars (environ 260 millions d’euros). L’Italie est la principale destination, absorbant 28 % des exportations, devant l’Espagne, la Libye, l’Algérie et le Japon. La mise en conformité des emballages constitue donc une étape essentielle pour éviter tout retard d’expédition, contestation documentaire ou difficulté d’accès au marché communautaire, notamment pour les crustacés, les mollusques, le poisson réfrigéré et les conserves, secteurs pour lesquels l’UE représente l’un des principaux débouchés commerciaux de la Tunisie. items.title: Osun election: Election is not warfare, stop militarising it — Accord tells FG
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Accord Party, on Friday, demanded the immediate resignation of the Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, accusing the anti-graft agency of partisanship and interference in the August 15 governorship election in Osun State. The party said the demand followed the EFCC’s now-reversed freezing of the Osun State Government’s bank account, which it described as the latest in a series of actions that had heightened fears of institutional interference in the state’s electoral process. Speaking at a world press conference in Abuja, Accord National Chairman, Chief Maxwell Mgbudem, said the party had lost confidence in the EFCC leadership and called on President Bola Tinubu to sack its chairman if he failed to resign. “Having demonstrated unprecedented partisanship in the Osun State politics, assaulted the sensibilities of fellow compatriots and brought the nation to ridicule and disrepute before the international community, Accord has lost confidence in the current leadership of the EFCC,” Mgbudem said. He accused the commission of exceeding its statutory mandate by freezing the state government’s account on August 5, saying the action threatened public confidence in democratic institutions. “Accordingly, Accord demands the immediate resignation of the EFCC chairman. For embarrassing the President, the Party, the Government and people of Osun State and fellow citizens. The EFCC chairman should toe the path of honour and tender his resignation. If he fails to resign, President Tinubu should sack him immediately to restore the integrity of the anti-graft agency,” the Accord chairman stated. The party chairman said the EFCC action came against the backdrop of what Accord described as months of political violence and intimidation in Osun, with members and supporters allegedly killed, shot, arrested, harassed and intimidated. Mgbudem also alleged that the offices of the Imole Campaign Council and the party in the state had been attacked, while campaign billboards were destroyed by suspected thugs linked to the All Progressives Congress, APC. According to him, Accord had reported the alleged attacks to security agencies and, in some cases, notified them ahead of planned incidents, but accused the authorities of failing to prevent the attacks or arrest those responsible. He said the party had initially welcomed the decision by the Inspector-General of Police to deploy a new Commissioner of Police to Osun following public concern over the security situation, but alleged that the EFCC’s intervention had subsequently aggravated the political atmosphere. Mgbudem said the development reinforced the party’s fears of an attempt to use federal institutions to weaken Governor Ademola Adeleke’s administration ahead of the election. “EFCC joined the Osun political fray hoping to succeed where the earlier compromised State Police Command failed by deliberately turning the law upside down to justify its unconstitutional action that threatened the foundations of the country’s emerging democracy,” he alleged. But he commended Tinubu for intervening after the Osun State Government, Accord and other Nigerians appealed to him, saying the President’s order for the immediate reversal of the account freeze had helped avert further escalation. “Accord welcomes President Tinubu’s timely intervention in this critical national issue and urges security agencies, anti-graft commissions, electoral umpire and relevant democratic institutions to strictly abide by their rules of engagement, statutory duties and democratic ethics,” Mgbudem said. He, however, warned the Federal Government against deploying state institutions in a manner that could compromise the August 15 poll. “Electoral contest is not a warfare. It should not be militarized by deploying federal apparatuses to suppress, subdue and oppress political opponents and their supporters to favour a party that has been rejected by the people,” he warned. He said Osun residents must be allowed to freely choose their governor, insisting that Accord would not bow to intimidation. The party chairman described Osun as an Accord stronghold and said Adeleke deserved a second term, citing his administration’s performance and what he called its delivery of dividends of democracy. Mgbudem also alleged that there had been previous attempts to destabilise the state government, including a court action seeking the deregistration of Accord and four other political parties. “It was to abruptly stop Adeleke’s transformative leadership that an attempt was made by the so-called former legislators to use the court to de-register Accord; four other political parties were merely added to cover-up their hidden agenda,” he said. He further alleged that the paralysis of local government operations and withholding of federal allocations to the councils were part of efforts to weaken Adeleke’s administration. According to him, those efforts had failed and would not stop the electorate from deciding the governor’s fate at the ballot box. The party urged Osun voters to come out in large numbers on August 15, vote for Adeleke and protect their ballots, insisting that every vote must be counted and reflected in the final result. It also charged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to conduct a free, fair, credible and inclusive election, describing the poll as particularly important because it would be the last off-cycle governorship election before the 2027 general elections. Accord urged INEC to adequately test its electoral materials and systems ahead of the poll, warning that glitches or operational failures could worsen an already tense political environment. The party called on the international community, civil society organisations, election observer missions, the Nigerian Bar Association, (NBA), the media, development partners, opposition political parties and other stakeholders to closely monitor the election and speak out against any conduct capable of undermining its credibility. It said the poll must be free from violence, intimidation, harassment, unlawful interference by security agencies, manipulation, voter suppression and vote-buying. Security agencies, Accord said, must remain professional and impartial, with their constitutional responsibility limited to protecting lives, maintaining law and order and providing a secure environment for voters. “The people of Osun State deserve nothing less than an election whose outcome genuinely reflects their freely expressed democratic choice,” the Accord chairman said. The party also appealed to Tinubu and the Inspector-General of Police to release what it described as the remaining 60 Accord members detained by the police in Abuja, Osun and Nasarawa states. Mgbudem said the release of the detainees would help reduce the political tension surrounding the election. He said Accord was fully prepared for the poll and expressed confidence that the party would emerge victorious on August 15. “Accord is ready and prepared for the governorship election and will emerge victorious having fulfilled its campaign promises to the people in spite of the activities of detractors to frustrate Adeleke’s government,” he declared. The post Osun election: Election is not warfare, stop militarising it — Accord tells FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pampaso chiefs invoke curses on Kumasi Mayor, Police Commander, Interior Minister over disputed land
items.description: The Pampaso Sub-Traditional Council in Kumasi has invoked traditional curses on the Mayor of Kumasi, Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, Ashanti Regional Police Commander, DCOP Arthur Osei Akoto, and the Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed Mubarak, over a disputed parcel of land the council claims belongs to the Pampaso Stool. According to the council, the land currently occupied by the Ashanti Regional Police Headquarters, Police bungalows, the Children’s Hospital area and adjoining properties was originally released by the Chief of Pampaso to the government strictly for public use. The chiefs, however, allege that the Ashanti Regional Police Command has expanded beyond the original boundaries and has allocated part of the disputed land to a private developer for the construction of shops. Speaking in an interview, the Pampaso Gyaasehene, Nana Obeng Afriyie, said the council has no objection to the portion of land lawfully granted to the government but strongly opposes what it describes as the unauthorised occupation of additional stool lands without the consent of either the Pampaso Stool or the Asantehene. He further alleged that the Ashanti Regional Police Commander and the Kumasi Mayor had previously appeared before the Traditional Council to justify the Police Service’s claim to the land but were unable to produce evidence proving the property belongs to the Police. Nana Obeng Afriyie also accused the officials of acting with the support of the Interior Minister to facilitate what he described as the unlawful takeover of the stool land. According to him, the council would not stand by while its ancestral lands were allegedly taken over without due process. As part of their protest, the chiefs performed traditional rites at the disputed site, slaughtering a sheep and invoking curses against the Ashanti Regional Police Commander, the Kumasi Mayor and the Interior Minister. The council said the ritual was intended to call the three officials before their ancestral gods to face spiritual consequences should they continue what the chiefs describe as the unlawful occupation of the land. The Pampaso Sub-Traditional Council maintained that it would continue to pursue both traditional and lawful means to protect the disputed stool lands. Mayor rejects allegations Responding to the claims, Kumasi Mayor Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi denied any involvement in the alleged takeover of the land. He said neither he nor the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) played any role in the construction of the alleged police shops on the disputed property or approved any private commercial development there. On the curses invoked against him, Mr Boadi said he remained unfazed, insisting he had done nothing wrong. “I am not scared of their curse because I have no involvement in the construction of the police stores in Adum-Pampaso,” he said. The Mayor described the chiefs’ actions as contrary to due process, arguing that any land dispute should be resolved through the appropriate traditional and legal channels rather than through spiritual sanctions. He also warned that he would report the chiefs involved in the ritual to the Asantehene if video evidence confirmed their participation. “I have not seen the video yet, and I will report members of the Adum-Pampaso Traditional Council who were involved to the Asantehene if I see video evidence of them cursing me,” he stated. Efforts by JoyNews to obtain responses from the Ashanti Regional Police Command and the Ministry of the Interior were unsuccessful at the time of filing this report.

items.title: Le diplomate russe Vassili Nebenzia dénonce l’implication de l’Ukraine dans des activités terroristes en Afrique
items.description: AFRIQUE-IMPLICATION-UKRAINE-TERRORISME Le diplomate russe Vassili Nebenzia dénonce l’implication de l'Ukraine dans des activités terroristes en Afrique Ouagadougou, 7 août 2026 (AIB) – Le représentant permanent de la Russie auprès de l'Organisation des Nations unies (ONU), Vassili Nebenzia, a dénoncé l'implication de l'Ukraine dans des activités terroristes sur le continent africain, notamment dans la livraison de drones et la formation directe de terroristes par des instructeurs militaires ukrainiens, lors d'une réunion du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU, tenue le mercredi 5 août 2026. Devant le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU, le diplomate russe Vassili Nebenzia a accusé le régime de Kiev de mener des activités terroristes en Afrique, évoquant des livraisons de drones, la formation de combattants par des instructeurs ukrainiens et la circulation d'armes occidentales vers des groupes armés dans plusieurs régions du monde. Selon lui, cette implication de l’Ukraine dans des activités terroristes en Afrique devrait faire l'objet d'une attention particulière, compte tenu de la situation sécuritaire dans plusieurs pays africains. Vassili Nebenzia a également déclaré que des armes occidentales livrées à l'Ukraine avaient été retrouvées entre les mains de groupes armés, non seulement en Afrique, mais aussi en Amérique latine et au Moyen-Orient. Il a ajouté que des organismes de contrôle américains s'interrogeaient sur l'utilisation de l'aide militaire accordée à Kiev sous l'administration de Joe Biden. Au-delà des activités attribuées à Kiev, Vassili Nebenzia a également mis en cause le rôle des pays occidentaux, qui, selon lui, utiliseraient l'Ukraine pour défendre leurs intérêts sur le continent africain, en particulier dans la région du Sahel. Le diplomate a affirmé que le soutien apporté par les Ukrainiens à des groupes terroristes servirait des objectifs géopolitiques plus larges. Il a indiqué que Moscou considérait ainsi que l'implication ukrainienne en Afrique ne pouvait être dissociée de la politique menée par les alliés occidentaux de Kiev. Ces accusations rejoignent plusieurs déclarations formulées récemment par de hauts responsables russes. Le directeur du département Afrique du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, Anatoli Bachkine, avait notamment déclaré, le 20 juillet, que des spécialistes ukrainiens participaient à la planification d'opérations menées par des groupes terroristes en Afrique. Le ministre russe des Affaires étrangères, Sergueï Lavrov, ainsi que d'autres responsables de Moscou, ont également affirmé que des combattants et des instructeurs ukrainiens étaient présents dans plusieurs pays du continent africain. Le Mali figure parmi les pays les plus directement concernés par ces déclarations. Selon un article publié par le média russe Gazeta, le 5 août 2026, un pilote de l'Africa Corps des forces russes a affirmé que des opérateurs ukrainiens de drones FPV participaient aux combats aux côtés des terroristes dans le pays. Le militaire a indiqué que cette présence avait été établie grâce à des interceptions radio et aux témoignages des terroristes capturés. Ces éléments viendraient renforcer les accusations formulées par Moscou au sujet des activités de Kiev dans la région du Sahel. Pour les autorités russes, l'ensemble de ces informations témoigne d'une implication croissante de l'Ukraine auprès des terroristes en Afrique. Elles soulèvent également la question du contrôle des armes occidentales fournies à Kiev et de leur circulation vers d'autres zones de conflit. Agence d’information du Burkina Source : RT

items.title: Police arrest 9 over GH¢30,000 mobile money robbery at Fiapre, two dead from shooting
items.description: The Bono Regional Police Command has arrested nine suspects in connection with the robbery of a mobile money vendor and the fatal shooting of a man at Fiapre-Zongo in the Sunyani West Municipality. The suspects are assisting police with investigations and will be processed for court, according to a statement signed by the Bono Regional Police Public Relations Officer, Chief Inspector Thomas Akeelah. The incident occurred on Wednesday, August 5, at about 8:00 p.m., when police received a distress call reporting an ongoing robbery at Fiapre. “Personnel responded swiftly to the scene; however, the perpetrators had fled before their arrival. The attack was targeted at a mobile money vendor,” the police said. Police identified the victims as Amina Abu, 30, the mobile money vendor, Khadija Abu, 23, Anifa Tanko, 24, and Ibrahim Osei, 40, all of whom sustained pellet wounds during the attack. During a search of the area, Police officers also found an unidentified man with severe injuries behind Ibrahim Osei’s house, with a black mask lying beside him. All five victims were rushed to the Sunyani Teaching Hospital for treatment. However, Ibrahim Osei died on arrival, while the unidentified man later died while receiving medical attention. The bodies of Ibrahim Osei and the unidentified man have been deposited at the hospital mortuary for preservation, identification and autopsy. Investigators indicated, according to the release, that Amina Abu was robbed of GH₵30,000 during the attack. Police also recovered six spent BB cartridge casings from the crime scene for forensic examination. According to the statement, preliminary investigations indicate that the suspects got off a cattle truck travelling towards Berekum before carrying out the robbery. “The Twumasikrom checkpoint on the Fiapre Berekum road was alerted to intercept two vehicles carrying cattle. Nine suspects have been arrested to assist with the investigation into the incident. They will be processed for prosecution,” the statement said. The Bono Regional Police Command says efforts are continuing to track down other suspects believed to have escaped. “The command assures the public that efforts are underway to apprehend the remaining perpetrators who are still at large and bring them to face the full rigours of the law,” Chief Inspector Thomas Akeelah stated. Meanwhile, Fiapre, which hosts a large number of students from the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR), has become a source of concern following the incident. The situation has sparked fear and anxiety among the student body, prompting the circulation of messages from the students’ leadership urging them to remain security-conscious. “If you are around the Fiapre Toll Booth area, please stay vigilant and avoid unnecessary movement,” the message advised. The student leadership further urged colleagues to “exercise extreme caution, avoid the area if possible, and follow updates from the security authorities. Stay safe and look out for one another.”

items.title: Kwara-Woro freed victims arrive Ilorin; children already enlisted in bandits army, says lawmaker
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin The victims abducted during the deadly attack on Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State have arrived in Ilorin following their rescue after spending several months in captivity. They reportedly arrived late last night. They were received at the Nigerian Army’s 2 Division, Sobi Barracks, Ilorin before being moved to an undisclosed location where they spent the night. The victims were kidnapped when armed bandits invaded the community February this year, killing scores of residents and whisking away many others into the forest, triggering widespread outrage and intensified security operations. Following sustained military operations and coordinated efforts by security agencies, the victims regained their freedom and were transported from Niger State to Ilorin late Thursday night. The rescued victims are expected to be officially handed over to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, who has consistently engaged security authorities to ensure their safe return. Their arrival marks a major breakthrough in the months-long efforts to secure the release of the abductees, while authorities continue to verify the number of those rescued and provide necessary care and support. Meanwhile Lawmaker representing Gwanabe/Gweria/Bani/Adena state constituency of Kaiama local government in the state House of Assembly, Hon. Saidu Baba-Ahmed,has said that some children among the 176 people kidnapped in Woro and Nukku communities of the Kaiama local government area of Kwara state on February 3, 2026 have been enlisted into the abductors’ army. He said this on Friday on the BBC Hausa service, monitored in Ilorin, adding that number of the rescued kidnap victims are not up to number of 176 people abducted. According to him, about 25 persons among the kidnapped persons are still missing, stressing that some are dead and buried by the abductees themselves. He said the remaining who are within the age of 13 years and above have been enlisted into the bandits’ army, “as explained by those who had returned home”. Hon. Saidu Baba-Ahmed said that those rescued arrived in Ilorin, the Kwara state capital, safe and are receiving medical attention. He said the state government is taking care of them to ascertain their state of health before reuniting them with their families. The lawmaker commended the state and the federal governments for their efforts in ensuring that the abductees return home safely. items.title: Ethiopia’s Addis Standard editor Yonas Kedir allegedly abducted as rights groups warn of media crackdown
items.description: The editor-in-chief of a leading Ethiopian independent news site was abducted and assaulted by security forces, according to its owner. The Addis Standard’s Yonas Kedir was taken last Saturday, held for 24 hours and subjected to “prolonged interrogation”, Jakken Publishing said in a statement on Thursday that also described a raid on the news site’s offices. Rights groups have described these latest incidents as part of a pattern of targeting independent news outlets. The Ethiopian government has not responded to a BBC request for comment. In February, the authorities revoked the Addis Standard’s media registration saying it had violated media ethics and what it described as threats to “national interests”, but did not specify which reports it was referring to. The news site was able to continue working as it was challenging the move in court. The alleged abduction of Yonas took place on the first of three days of action against the Addis Standard, Jakken Publishing said. “Two individuals dressed in civilian clothes… violently seized me,” the AFP news agency quotes Yonas as saying in a written statement. “[They] struck me and forcibly loaded me into a double-cab pickup truck. They accused me of ‘selling the country out’.” On the second day, Sunday 2 August, a security team raided the outlet’s offices “without due process”, Jakken Publishing said, confiscating equipment from its multimedia studio. Then on 3 August, police issued an eviction order requiring the company to vacate its premises within three days, ending 16 years of operations at the site. The Addis Standard’s website is still available and is being updated with reports on the raid and its aftermath. The publisher is currently consulting on what to do next. The Committee to Protect Journalists has described what happened as part of “an alarming escalation in Ethiopian authorities’ campaign to dismantle one of the country’s leading independent news organisations”. Human Rights Watch (HRW) also criticised the government’s actions, saying the harassment of the Addis Standard reflects a broader effort to silence critical reporting. HRW noted that in the past year, Ethiopian authorities have arbitrarily arrested scores of journalists, held some incommunicado, and revoked media licences. The Ethiopian Media Authority recently issued “final written warnings” to independent broadcasters Arts TV and Ahadu FM, threatening suspension or revocation of their licences after alleging repeated violations of media laws.

items.title: Norway call for Infantino to resign as Mexico and Argentina back president
items.description: Norway have called on Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign following his aborted attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, but Mexico and Argentina have voiced their support for the 56-year-old. Norway have gone a step further than the football associations of England, Wales, Croatia and Albania, all of whom have withdrawn support for Infantino without explicitly calling for him to resign. “He [Infantino] does not have the institutional trust required to govern Fifa stably in the times we are in,” Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness said on Friday. “There is no going back for Gianni Infantino. The international football cooperation is very much in trouble, and we must have a reason to get together now, and we want to ask the Fifa president to resign now. “We will see which other countries eventually join in, if that becomes the strategy from the Uefa board. We are not going to ask for an extraordinary [Uefa board] meeting, we will ask him to resign in our dialogue with Fifa.” Klaveness, who is a qualified lawyer, went through a list of concerns that the Norwegian FA has expressed to Fifa during her four-year tenure. Among them were questions around the awarding of tournaments, the inaugural Fifa peace prize that was awarded to US President ​Donald Trump in December, and the overturning of a ban for American forward Folarin Balogun during the recent World Cup following a phone call from Trump. Meanwhile, earlier on Friday the Mexican Football Federation broke ranks with its regional governing body Concacaf to come out in support of Infantino. Concacaf, which runs football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, called for a “comprehensive reckoning” of Infantino’s presidency after he aborted plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. However, 2026 World Cup co-hosts Mexico have backed Infantino’s leadership amid widespread calls for him to resign. “The FMF [Mexican FA] supports president Infantino’s leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening,” a statement read. It echoed a statement from Conmebol – South America’s governing body – in saying it would reject any attempt to remove Infantino without a vote involving all 211 Fifa members. “The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made by president Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations,” it added. However, Conmebol did “express its concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue or the institutional mechanisms provided for dealing with this type of situation”. Meanwhile, the football association of 2026 World Cup runners-up Argentina praised Infantino for recognising and apologising for his “errors”. It described his decade-long tenure as Fifa president as “centred on the development of soccer worldwide and institutional strength based on a clear, stable, and transparent governance model”. Infantino is unanimously backed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), but faces opposition from European football’s governing Uefa and Concacaf. European teams could still boycott the World Cup as Uefa said its conditions had not been met, despite Infantino’s plan being aborted. “Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again,” a Uefa statement read. “These conditions have not been met.” Uefa has already said it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal a “shabby, back room, opaque deal”. The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino, while Wales, Albania and Croatia are among other individual associations to have turned their back on the 56-year-old. Concacaf described Infantino’s proposal as “a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first”, and that “this recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour”. However, unlike Uefa, it did not go as far as to say it had lost confidence in the Fifa president. Before Infantino withdrew his proposal, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it stood “in solidarity” with Uefa and Concacaf in opposition to the plans. Figure caption,Why Uefa could still boycott the World Cup Infantino had offered all associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups, through the FFE subsidiary. During a meeting of Fifa executives in Morocco on Wednesday, the world governing body said “mistakes” regarding FFE were “acknowledged”, saying it was “not the intention” for the Fifa Council and members association to “feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently”. Uefa’s statement in response added: “Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds. “Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.” Fifa has been approached for comment.

items.title: Trump imposes 15% tariff on key chip material to counter China
items.description: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Thursday that imposes a 15% tariff on imported products made from polysilicon, a crucial material used in semiconductors and solar panels. The order also set minimum import prices on polysilicon and related products. It comes after a national security investigation into the production of the material overseas. The move is intended to help protect US manufacturers as they face increasing competition from China’s chip industry – a key source of friction between the world’s two largest economies. The Chinese embassy in Washington said the move “seriously disrupts” trade between the two countries and Beijing will act to protect its companies. Washington is “abusing state power to go after Chinese businesses,” the embassy said, adding that protectionism will not make the US more competitive. Trump said in the order that he had accepted recommendations by Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to set minimum import prices as well as a 15% tariff on polysilicon and related imports. The measures are due to take effect in December. The US will also offer incentives to boost domestic production, it added. For decades, the US has allowed “foreign firms to weaken United States producers in the polysilicon sector,” said Trump, who has long advocated for the use of tariffs to protect American jobs and boost the economy. The material is critical in military equipment and electronics, yet imports have led to the US’ share of global polysilicon production to fall from 50% in 2005 to less than 2% in 2024, Trump said. China holds a near monopoly on the production of polysilicon. The order is likely to benefit Hemlock Semiconductor and Wacker Chemie, which are the main producers of the material in the US. The production of computer chips is central to the race between the US and China to develop artificial intelligence (AI). Washington and Beijing have also been locked in a tit-for-tat tariffs war, which has been on hold since May 2025. Analysts quoted by Chinese state media outlet Global Times said the new tariff marks the latest escalation in Washington’s efforts to limit China’s role in critical technology supply chains. The move follows other US restrictions on the imports of drones, humanoid robots and other tech products from China. China announced a range of countermeasures this week, including tighter export controls on drones. Beijing also launched a national security review into imported printers and copiers.

items.title: Seven killed after Thai teen shooter opens fire at home and school
items.description: At least sevenpeople have been killed and more than 30 injured after a 14-year-old boy opened fire at his home and school on the outskirts of Thailand’s capital Bangkok. The student killed his grandparents and five teachers before taking his own life, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters. The attacker still had “more than 30 bullets left” when he turned the gun on himself, the PM added. Nine of the injured people remain in a critical condition, authorities added. The school in Nonthaburi province is a local branch of the renowned Debsirin School, which in Thailand is widely associated with educational prestige. Police were deployed to the scene during the active shooting. National police chief police general Kittiratt Phanphet told reporters that forensic officers had found the gunman’s shots were quite accurate, with several hitting the vital spots on the body. The PM said the attack was “well prepared” with “clear steps and clear goals”. The attacker has not been publicly named. Authorities earlier warned people to stay away from the area and for those in trapped in the building to hide and wait for rescuers. At one point police warned in a social media post that the shooter was in the school’s computer room. The Debsirin School, founded in Bangkok in 1885, is one of Thailand’s top secondary schools with branches across the country. It counts many prominent Thai figures as its alumni, from diplomats and athletes to several prime ministers. A seventh-grade student, who fled the building, told the BBC that she was in class when she saw the gunman walking from room to room. When he reached her classroom, he shot the teacher standing near the entrance, she said. She added that she couldn’t see anything else after that. Another student told Reuters that he had thought the sound of gunshots were firecrackers going off, or someone banging an object. “There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again.” The 9mm handgun used by the shooter belonged to his grandfather, a former teacher, police said. Students and school staff were seen fleeing from the scene, and those waiting outside the Debsirin school looked visibly distraught. 0:59Students shelter in classroom as gunshots heard In a post on social media, the school later shared a call for blood donations. Other schools in the vicinity suspended classes so students could return home early. PM Charnvirakul expressed condolences for the victims of the school shooting. He said the tragedy “shouldn’t have happened”, adding “this is why the government do not allow [citizens] to possess firearms”. “I don’t just feel sorry for the victims but I feel sorry that this happened. How can this happen in our country,” he said. Thailand has strict gun laws, which punishes the illegal possession of arms with up to 10 years in jail. But enforcement of these laws has been an issue. The country has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in South East Asia. It is estimated that about 40% of these guns are illegal.

The memorial was unveiled at the Ministry of Defence on Thursday, August 6, in remembrance of Dr Omane Boamah and the other victims of the tragic incident. Paying tribute to his former aide and confidant, President Mahama described Dr Omane Boamah as “a friend, a younger brother, a loyalist and a close adviser” whose commitment and loyalty remained unquestionable throughout their political journey. “He stood by my side through all the momentous occasions of my political career,” President Mahama said. The President said the late Defence Minister played a significant role in his political career and remained dedicated to public service until his passing. Dr Edward Omane Boamah was among the eight victims who died when a Ghana Armed Forces helicopter crashed in the Adansi area of the Ashanti Region on August 6, 2025. The anniversary commemoration brought together government officials, family members, security personnel and other dignitaries to honour the memory of those who lost their lives.

items.title: ‘My son will be bigger than me’ – Ronaldo
items.description: Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo has predicted that his eldest son, Cristiano Jr., could surpass him in football, saying the teenager is already physically ahead of where he was at the same age. The 41-year-old made the comments in a video shared by Netflix Sports while watching his 16-year-old son train with the Al Nassr youth team. Ronaldo said Cristiano Jr. has developed physically beyond where he was at the same age and bel ieves his son could eventually grow bigger and stronger than him. “He’s a good kid. The other ones are tougher, the ones at home, the small ones. This one is no problem,” Ronaldo said. “When I was his age, he is a little bit bigger and stronger. I was smaller. I think he will be bigger than me.” However, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner acknowledged that physical development and talent alone would not guarantee his son success at the highest level. Ronaldo was also asked whether Cristiano Jr. would develop the same hunger and mentality that helped him become one of the greatest footballers of all time. The Portugal captain identified hunger as one of the most difficult qualities to develop. “Hunger is the most difficult,” he said. Cristiano Jr., born on June 17, 2010, currently plays for the Al Nassr youth team as he continues to follow in his father’s footsteps. Ronaldo has enjoyed a decorated career, winning five Ballon d’Or awards and five UEFA Champions League titles, as well as the European Championship with Portugal in 2016. The veteran forward has also won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia and remains the leading goalscorer in men’s international football. With Cristiano Jr. progressing through the Al Nassr system, attention will continue to focus on whether he can establish a career of his own and potentially surpass the extraordinary achievements of his father. items.title: La commune Tchaoudjo 4 bientôt dotée de son PDC
items.description: Sokodé, 7 août (ATOP) – La commune Tchaoudjo 4 a officiellement lancé, le jeudi 6 août à Kpassouadè, l’élaboration de son Plan de développement communal (PDC), une feuille de route stratégique permettant de fixer les priorités d’investissement et de stimuler la croissance durable et participative. Ce PDC est un document de planification couvrant une période de cinq ans et élaboré sur la base d’une méthodologie qui intègre toutes les prévisions et programmations d’ordre social, économique, culturel, spatial, environnemental et autres de la commune. Il ambitionne de faire de ladite commune un exemple inspirant de planification territoriale intégrée, conciliant développement économique et préservation de l’environnement. Son élaboration requiert la participation et l’implication de tous les acteurs du développement de la municipalité. Le processus bénéficie de l’appui du Programme « Restauration des paysages forestiers et bonne gouvernance dans le secteur forestier » (Forests4furure). Ce programme est cofinancé par l’Allemagne et le Luxembourg et mis en œuvre par la GIZ. M. Bawo mettant en terre son plan L’appui à l’élaboration de cet outil stratégique de développement sera exécuté en cinq phases constituée, chacune, de plusieurs étapes. Ces phases portent sur la préparation, la définition de la vision, des orientations stratégiques, des objectifs et des résultats attendus. Elles intègrent la programmation, la rédaction et la validation du plan puis son adoption par le Conseil municipal et son approbation par le préfet. Durant ce processus, les parties prenantes échangeront sur le développement de cette localité, notamment les enjeux, les forces, les faiblesses et les perspectives en vue d’élaborer un PDC qui reflète la réalité de la commune et les aspirations de ses populations. Au cours de l’atelier, elles ont suivi les grandes étapes du processus d’élaboration du PDC ainsi que la présentation des membres du comité de pilotage et du cabinet d’appui. Elles ont été éclairées sur le contexte de mise en œuvre du programme Forests4Future en lien avec la planification du développement. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Tchaoudjo, Bawo Moukadassi, le représentant du ministère délégué chargé du Développement local, Faligbene Likfière et le directeur régional de l’Environnement, Lt-Col. Alèdi Palakyèm ont insisté sur l’approche participative et inclusive dans l’élaboration de ce plan. Ils ont rassuré de la disponibilité de leur structure à apporter leurs appuis techniques nécessaires pour la réussite de ce processus. Ces autorités ont invité chaque acteur à œuvrer au renforcement de la cohésion dans sa communauté afin de maintenir un climat de paix et de sécurité indispensable à la réussite du PDC. Le maire de la commune Tchaoudjo 4, Kpégouni Tchagnao a réitéré l’engagement des autorités communales à jouer leur partition depuis l’enquête jusqu’à la finalisation du processus en passant par les foras communautaires et autres. Le conseiller technique de Forests4Future /GIZ, Dr Koumantiga Dabitora a rappelé que le PDC de Tchaoudjo 4 s’inscrit dans une dynamique plus large qui concerne également les communes Tchaoudjo 2 et Sotouboua 3. Il a invité les collectivités territoriales, les services de l’Etat et les populations à travailler dans un esprit de collaboration, de transparence et d’innovation pour construire des territoires plus résilients, plus productifs et plus durables. La rencontre a pris fin par une opération de mis en terre de plan. ATOP/MEK/HKM/KYA
