items.title: Nigerian man jailed 13 months after high-speed police chase, multiple crashes in UK
items.description: A 23-year-old Nigerian man has been sentenced to 13 months in prison after admitting to dangerous driving during a high-speed police chase in Northampton, UK. Michael Chiedu Nwanze was arrested by police in Abington Square, Northampton, on March 10, after officers flagged down the vehicle he was driving for having no insurance. Instead of stopping, Nwanze fled, triggering a pursuit through Cheyne Walk and Bedford Road before continuing onto the A45. Police eventually brought the chase to an end near Wellingborough after Nwanze encountered stationary traffic at the Wilby Way roundabout. During the pursuit, he reportedly ran several red lights, reached speeds of 70mph in 40mph zones and exceeded 100mph while travelling on the dual carriageway. His attempt to escape came to an end when he collided with several vehicles while trying to navigate through the stationary traffic. Officers subsequently boxed in his vehicle, allowing them to arrest him. Nwanze was charged with several offences, including dangerous driving, driving without insurance, driving otherwise than in accordance with a licence and failing to stop for police. He pleaded guilty to the offences at Northampton Crown Court in April before returning to the same court in June, where he was sentenced to 13 months in prison. Lead investigator PC Thomas Williams, from Northamptonshire Police’s Roads Policing Team, said: “As you can see from the footage, Nwanze’s actions that day showed a complete disregard for the safety of other road users and pedestrians. “During the pursuit, he drove at excessive speeds, ignored traffic signals and put countless people at risk in an attempt to avoid being stopped by officers. “Dangerous driving of this nature can have devastating consequences, and it is only by good fortune that nobody was seriously injured as a result of his behaviour that day. “We will continue to proactively target those who use our roads illegally and dangerously, and I hope this sentence sends a clear message that this type of offending will not be tolerated.” Vanguard News The post Nigerian man jailed 13 months after high-speed police chase, multiple crashes in UK appeared first on Vanguard News .

Canal controversy
items.description: RECENTLY put into trial operation , Jalalpur canal has stoked a new controversy between Punjab and Sindh. A summary of the Sindh government, raising objections against the project, was already pending with the Council of Common Interests (CCI) since 2024. Sindh had been raising objections on this project from its inception, but these have been consistently disregarded. A 117km-long main canal with a design discharge of 1,350 cusecs off-taking from the right bank of the Rasul barrage on the Jhelum river, it aims to irrigate a culturable command area of about 68,000 hectares in the Potohar plateau of Punjab, mainly in Pind Dadan Khan and Khushab during the Kharif season. The Asian Development Bank had provided financial assistance for design and construction of the project to the Punjab government. Punjab claims that it will use its own share of water for the new canal through internal adjustment. Sindh, however, has questioned the source of additional water of approximately 0.5 million acre feet every year. Punjab has distributed all its water allocated under the 1991 Water Accord. Internal adjustment would require slashing the share of water of some other canal command area. Publicly available project documents do not mention barrages or canals willing to sacrifice their share of water. Diverting allocated water will deprive the command area concerned of its irrigation share. The Indus River System Authority (Irsa), while issuing a no-objection certificate for the project in September 2014, made it contingent upon using Punjab’s own share of water for the canal. The Sindh member was the only dissenting voice, but was outvoted with a majority of 4-1. Irsa, however, did not question how Punjab will internally adjust allocation of water of its canals without any detriment to the existing command areas. The project envisages a significantly above-normal water allowance. It is also noteworthy that the project envisages a significantly above-normal water allowance. The canal has been designed with a water allowance of approximately 6.75 cusecs per thousand acres, nearly two-and-a-half times higher than the 2.75 cusecs per thousand acres allowance for Sindh’s canal systems. The provincial assembly of Sindh, in its sitting on November 22, 2021, unanimously adopted a resolution moved by Jam Khan Shoro, minister for irrigation, and several other members to express grave concern over the construction of the Jalalpur canal and Chaubara branch canal project under greater Thal canal (phase-II). The resolution also criticised the federal government for its alleged compliance with the controversial project despite the legal objections of Sindh. The house termed the project against the 1991 Water Accord and the Irsa Act, 1992. Prior to this, the Sindh government through P&D department raised the objection in the Ecnec meeting held in early 2018. The provincial government also addressed a letter to the secretary, ministry of planning, development and special initiatives on Nov 11, 2021 to convey reservations on the Jalalpur canal. The canal is designed to provide irrigation from April to October on non-perennial basis. The early Kharif months of April and May are a critical period when the Indus river system experiences severe water shortages. In its summary submitted to the CCI, Sindh has presented data on water shortages over the last two decades. The province witnessed over 50 per cent shortages in early Kharif for several years. In the current year too, Sindh experienced up to 65pc shortages at Kotri barrage during early Kharif months. A further diversion of 1,350 cusecs tro­ugh Jalalpur can­al will unleash havoc for crops in Sindh where Kha­­rif crops are sown earlier than Punjab. Sindh has apprehensions that since Punjab does not have any surplus water in the system, eventually it will divert additional water from the Indus through Chashma-Jhelum and Taunsa-Panjnad link canals to meet additional water requirements in the Jhelum zone. The Indus delta will ultimately pay the cost, which already receives little or no freshwater for much of the year and faces unrelenting ecological degradation. Further curtailment of freshwater inflows will worsen its fragile ecosystem by accelerating seawater intrusion and loss of livelihoods for the delta dwellers. CCI is a constitutional forum empowered to resolve conflicts on water sharing between the provinces under Article 154 of the Constitution. It is lamentable that the canal was constructed while Sindh’s summary awaited intervention of the CCI. The very act was in contravention of the spirit of the federation. Such instances undermine credibility of institutions like Irsa and the CCI and deepen mistrust between the federation and the federating units. The writer is a water sector expert. nmemon2004@yahoo.com Published in Dawn, August 7th, 2026

items.title: ‘Our forests are breathing again’ – Armah Buah honours Murtala Mohammed’s environmental legacy
items.description: The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources and Acting Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Emmanuel Armah Kofi Buah, has paid tribute to the late Dr Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed, describing his leadership in the repeal of Legislative Instrument (LI) 2462 as one of the defining achievements of his time in office. Speaking at a memorial ceremony held at the Ministry to mark one year since the former Environment Minister passed in a Ghana Armed Forces helicopter crash, Mr Armah Buah said Dr Muhammed’s commitment to protecting Ghana’s natural resources continues to shape government policy. He said the repeal of LI 2462, which had allowed mining in forest reserves under certain conditions, was a landmark decision that has strengthened efforts to protect the country’s forests. Reflecting on the late minister’s contribution, Mr Armah Buah said that the impact of the decision is already being felt. “He is the one that spearheaded the repeal of LI 2462. And today, our forests are breathing again because of Honourable Murtala. We can clap for him.” The ceremony brought together family members, friends, colleagues and government officials to honour Dr Muhammed and the seven others who died in the helicopter crash in the Ashanti Region on August 6, 2025. Mr Armah Buah said Dr Muhammed’s vision for environmental protection extended far beyond the repeal of LI 2462. He recalled that the late minister hosted the African Research Initiative for Scientific Excellence (ARISE) High-Level Meeting in 2025, which resulted in the Accra Declaration, and also introduced the Biannual Environment, Science and Technology Forum to strengthen collaboration between researchers, innovators and industry. According to him, the initiative was designed to ensure research produced practical solutions that would improve the lives of Ghanaians. “He wanted to make sure that research work was not an isolated issue, that it was practical, that the things people were researching into were really connected with the people of Ghana and that we could use them to transform our lives.” The Minister said the forum has now become a permanent feature of the ministry’s calendar because of its importance. He also credited Dr Muhammed with laying the foundation for Ghana’s Blue Economy Strategy, which has since been advanced by the Ministry of Fisheries, and for launching the One Child, One Tree campaign to encourage environmental responsibility among young people. “He also launched what we call the One Child, One Tree campaign to make sure that we instil environmental responsibility in our children right from an early age and make sure that every child knew the importance of planting trees.” The Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, also paid tribute to the late minister, saying the pain of losing him and the seven others remains deeply felt one year after the tragedy. He said the most meaningful way to honour their memory is to continue the fight to protect Ghana’s environment and natural resources. “Mohammed Murtala Mohammed. A year on, our heart is still in ruins. Our heart is still in ruins.” Mr Iddrisu said Dr Muhammed viewed environmental protection not simply as a government responsibility but as a moral duty. “For Murtala Mohammed, the protection of the environment, ensuring that our water quality, air quality was good enough, was moral.” He urged Ghanaians to remain committed to tackling illegal mining and protecting the country’s natural resources. “The best we can do to his memory and the memory of Dr Omane Boamah and all the eight is to preserve and protect the environment, to endeavour to succeed in fighting galamsey in order that we don’t compromise our water bodies, our farmlands and our air quality.” Dr Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed was among eight people who lost their lives when a Ghana Armed Forces Z-9 helicopter crashed while travelling to the launch of the government’s Cooperative Mining Initiative in the Ashanti Region.

items.title: Why Nigerians remain in Saudi prisons after serving jail terms — Envoy
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde Nigeria’s Ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Dr. Yakubu N. Gambo, has raised concerns over the plight of Nigerians who remain in Saudi prisons and detention centres even after completing their jail terms because they are unable to pay outstanding fines. Gambo disclosed this on Thursday during a visit to the Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission, NiDCOM, Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, at the Commission’s headquarters in Abuja. In a statement signed by NiDCOM’s Media, Public Relations and Protocol Violet Nwosu, the ambassador said addressing diaspora issues had remained a priority since he assumed office, noting that Nigeria’s foreign policy places significant emphasis on the welfare of citizens abroad. Ambassador Gambo said the Mission had directed the various Nigerian groups in Saudi Arabia to come together under one umbrella body to promote unity and enable the Embassy to engage them more effectively. “The mission has directed the various Nigerian groups to organise themselves under one umbrella body to foster unity and enable the Embassy to engage meaningfully and effectively in addressing any diaspora issue,” he said. The ambassador also drew attention to the plight of some Nigerians in the Kingdom. “We are also confronted with challenges involving Nigerians in prisons and detention centres, including those who have completed their jail terms but are unable to return home because of outstanding fines,” he added. Meanwhile, Gambo said contrary to widespread perceptions, Saudi Arabia is home to many successful Nigerian professionals, including doctors, engineers, teachers, artisans and traders, as well as families that have lived in the Kingdom for decades. He said the Nigerian Mission had directed the various Nigerian associations in Saudi Arabia to unite under one umbrella body to promote cohesion and enable the Embassy to engage more effectively in resolving issues affecting Nigerians. Speaking at the meeting, Nigeria’s Consul General in Jeddah, Ambassador Muazam I.J. Nayaya, described consular services as one of the mission’s biggest challenges, revealing that officials issue dozens of emergency travel certificates, ETCs, daily to Nigerians in detention centres seeking to return home. Nayaya also commended NiDCOM for its support in resolving the case involving Nigerian national Suleiman Alufa and other interventions on behalf of Nigerians in Saudi Arabia. Responding, Dabiri-Erewa assured the delegation of NiDCOM’s continued collaboration with the Nigerian Mission to strengthen engagement with Nigerians in the Kingdom and improve their welfare. She commended the Mission’s efforts to unite Nigerian associations in Saudi Arabia, describing the initiative as a step towards more effective engagement with the diaspora. The NiDCOM boss also lamented that the achievements of many Nigerians in Saudi Arabia often go unnoticed. “We only hear about the bad cases; we don’t hear about Nigerians excelling in Saudi Arabia. Now is the time to start celebrating them,” she said. Dabiri-Erewa urged Nigerians residing in Saudi Arabia to register on the Commission’s Diaspora Data Mapping Portal to enhance planning and engagement, while also calling for greater support for Nigerian missions handling increasing consular responsibilities. Both NiDCOM and the Nigerian Mission reaffirmed their commitment to protecting the welfare of Nigerians in Saudi Arabia and strengthening diaspora participation in Nigeria’s national development. The post Why Nigerians remain in Saudi prisons after serving jail terms — Envoy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Toke Makinwa unveils daughter Yakira’s face on first birthday
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Media personality Toke Makinwa has unveiled the face of her daughter, Yakira Eliana, as the little girl marked her first birthday. Makinwa shared a series of photographs of Yakira on social media Friday, giving fans and colleagues their first public glimpse of the child, whom she had largely kept away from the spotlight since her birth. Celebrating the milestone, the media personality described her daughter as her “answered prayer” and greatest blessing, reflecting on her journey into motherhood. “The best part of my story, finally yours to meet. Yakira Eliana. My precious answered prayer. My greatest love. My greatest blessing,” she wrote. Makinwa added that she was sharing “a little piece of my heaven with the world” as her daughter clocked one. “God can be trusted, God is real… Just like Hagar my mouth can testify that I have met ‘El-roi’, the God who sees me,” she added. In a playful message to her followers, Makinwa introduced Yakira as their “niece” while gushing over the little girl’s appearance. “Guys, meet your niece. I cooked ohhhhhh. She is beautiful,” she wrote. She also affectionately referred to her daughter by several nicknames, including YaYa, Ya Pom Pom and Ya Mama. The birthday post quickly attracted reactions from fans and celebrities, many of whom described Yakira as adorable and wished her a blessed new year. One follower described her as “a baby doll”, while actress Adunni Ade wrote, “She is gorgeous. Happy Birthday mommy’s girl.” Other reactions included birthday wishes and comments praising the child’s appearance. Makinwa’s decision to unveil Yakira’s face comes after a year of keeping details about her daughter relatively private. The birthday celebration has now offered her followers a closer look at the child she described as one of the greatest blessings of her life. items.title: Tunisie | Restauration et réaffectation d’édifices religieux abandonnés
items.description: La Tunisie a lancé un recensement des églises et synagogues dans les différentes régions du pays, dans le but de clarifier leur statut juridique et foncier et faire un l’état des bâtiments. Un plan d’entretien, de restauration et de mise en valeur est prévu ainsi que de nouvelles affectations pour des activités à caractère culturelle. (Photo: Eglises catholiques de Sfax et Gabès). Selon un communiqué du ministère des Affaires culturelles — qui ne précise pas le nombre total de biens concernés —, ce travail devra permettre d’actualiser les informations disponibles sur chaque bâtiment, d’en vérifier la situation juridique et d’identifier les éventuels problèmes liés à la propriété, à l’affectation ou aux modalités de gestion. Ce recensement servira également à établir un ordre de priorité pour les interventions, en tenant compte des caractéristiques architecturales et historiques de chaque édifice. Le programme prévoit des contrôles des infrastructures ainsi que la mise en place d’opérations d’entretien périodique ou de restauration, dans le respect des normes techniques applicables à la conservation des monuments historiques. Il s’agit de renforcer le nettoyage, l’entretien et le suivi régulier de ces sites, considérés comme faisant partie intégrante de la mémoire nationale et comme un témoignage de la pluralité culturelle et religieuse ayant marqué l’histoire de la Tunisie. Sont concernés de nombreux édifices construits à différentes époques et qui ne sont pas toujours affectés au culte aujourd’hui. Dans plusieurs cas, les autorités envisagent leur transformation en bibliothèques, médiathèques ou espaces culturels. Parmi les projets encore à l'étude figure la reconversion de l’ancienne église Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul de Sfax, construite entre 1940 et 1953, un chantier lancé en 2016 mais ralenti par des problèmes techniques et fonciers. En mars dernier, le ministère a annoncé la création d’un comité de pilotage chargé de relancer les travaux et de définir un nouveau calendrier opérationnel. L’ancienne église de Gabès, construite à partir de 1886, précédemment utilisée comme bibliothèque publique, est aussi concernée. Inscrit en janvier 2024 à l’inventaire des monuments du gouvernorat, l’édifice nécessite, selon le ministère, une régularisation de son statut foncier ainsi que des travaux structurels avant de pouvoir rouvrir au public. L’église Santa Croce, construite en 1837 dans la médina de Tunis, constitue un précédent significatif : restaurée grâce à la contribution de la Coopération italienne, elle a été reconvertie en espace culturel municipal. L’ensemble accueille aujourd’hui des expositions, des ateliers et des spectacles, tout en préservant les éléments principaux de son architecture d’origine. Ce patrimoine religieux pluriel figure également parmi les éléments ayant conduit, en 2023, à l’inscription de Djerba sur la liste du patrimoine mondial de l’Unesco. Outre les mosquées historiques de l’île, le dossier inclut la synagogue de la Ghriba ainsi que les églises catholique et orthodoxe, considérées comme l’expression de la stratification culturelle et religieuse du pays. Les autorités parlent de d’assurer une gestion pérenne de ces édifices qui, même lorsqu’ils ne conservent plus leur fonction religieuse initiale, demeurent partie intégrante du patrimoine historique et architectural tunisien. I. B. L’article Tunisie | Restauration et réaffectation d’édifices religieux abandonnés est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Cinkassé/campagne de reboisement : 33.097 plants distribués dans trois cantons de la préfecture
items.description: Cinkassé, 7 août. (ATOP) – Les cantons de Boadé et Gloungoussi dans la commune Cinkassé 1 et Sam-naba dans la commune Cinkassé 2, ont bénéficié de divers plants, dans le cadre de la campagne nationale de reboisement, le jeudi 6 août dans lesdites localités. Ces plants sont offerts par l’ONG Handicap International en collaboration avec la direction préfectorale de l’Environnement de Cinkassé, dans le cadre du projet « Bâtir et reconstruire les infrastructures pour la cohésion sociale (BRICS) » piloté avec l’appui financier de la Fondation PATRIP. Elle vise à accompagner le gouvernement dans la mise en œuvre de la campagne nationale de reboisement pour une lutte plus efficace contre la dégradation du couvert végétal au Togo. Il s’agit également de contribuer à l’atteinte de la vision gouvernementale de planter un milliard d’arbres à l’horizon 2030. Une partie des plants à distribuer Au total 33.097 plants composés de cacia, de leucenats, d’anacardes, de Kayas, de nérés et de manguiers ont été remis aux bénéficiaires à raison de 14.151 plants pour le canton de Sam-naba, 12.500 pour Gloungoussi et 6.446 pour le canton de Boadé. Le directeur préfectoral de l’Environnement de Cinkassé, Lieutenant Sambiani Betiandame a donné des conseils techniques aux bénéficiaires sur comment planter et entretenir pour faciliter la survie de ces arbres. Les autorités locales et les bénéficiaires ont exprimé leur gratitude à l’ONG Handicap International pour cette action et ont promis de mettre tout en œuvre pour la réussite de ce reboisement. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence des autorités locales, des acteurs impliqués dans la mise en œuvre du projet ainsi que des populations bénéficiaires. ATOP/BB/JK/MD

items.title: Kindi : le Conseil d’établissement reverdit la cour du lycée départemental

Mobilisés dès les premières heures de la journée, les membres du conseil du lycée, épaulés par des membres de la veille citoyenne et des élèves, ont procédé à la mise en terre de plusieurs plants. L'opération a permis de planter diverses espèces végétales, notamment des manguiers, des goyaviers, des neems et des eucalyptus, contribuant ainsi à l’embellissement et au reverdissement du temple du savoir. Le porte-parole des bénéficiaires a salué la mobilisation et l'engagement de l'ensemble des acteurs. Tout en exprimant sa gratitude aux participants pour leur soutien indéfectible, il a pris l'engagement ferme d'assurer l'entretien et le suivi régulier des plants mis en terre afin de garantir leur survie. items.title: Greater Accra Minister gives developers, occupants at Kpeshie Lagoon 21 days to vacate
items.description: The Greater Accra Regional Minister, Linda Ocloo has given residents and property owners encroaching on the Kpeshie Lagoon buffer zone at Laboma Beach a 21-day ultimatum to vacate or remove their structures or face demolition. The minister made the announcement during an inspection of the area, describing the exercise as part of ongoing efforts to reclaim waterways and address perennial flooding. “We are here purposely because of the ongoing flooding within the river,” the minister said. “We did a demolition exercise some time ago. It doesn’t mean that we stopped… Today, we are here to support them to make sure that we reclaim our waterway.” She disclosed that authorities had intended to begin demolitions immediately but decided to grant residents more time after learning that occupants had not received sufficient notice. “Honestly, we were here to do the exercise, but on second thought, we were told that the occupants have not been given enough notice,” she said. “We are giving them 21 days.” The minister warned that all structures within the designated buffer zone must be removed before the deadline. “Those buildings that fall within the buffer should be ready within 21 days. Either they demolish them themselves, or REGSEC will come back to demolish them,” she stated. She explained that restoring the buffer zone is critical to improving drainage and reducing flood risks in nearby communities. “We are going to create a kind of buffer to make sure that when it rains, that is where the chunk of the water settles and then gradually flows into the sea. We want to get back that waterway,” she said. The minister attributed recent flooding, including incidents in Tse Addo, to increasing encroachment on waterways. “For the first time, we heard that Tse Addo got flooded. It’s because of the encroachment,” she said. “We didn’t prevent anybody from developing the place but at least give some kind of space so that when it rains, the water can flow.” Authorities are currently assessing all structures within the Kpeshie Lagoon buffer zone ahead of the planned demolition exercise once the 21-day notice expires. This comes as a response by the government in addressing and controlling the effects of the floods especially after the casualties recorded on June 29, 2026.

items.title: OpenAI supprime les limites des conversations textuelles sur ChatGPT pour les utilisateurs gratuits
items.description: OpenAI franchit une nouvelle étape dans le développement de son assistant conversationnel. À partir de la semaine prochaine, les utilisateurs de la version gratuite de ChatGPT ainsi que les abonnés à l'offre Go pourront échanger de manière illimitée avec le chatbot pour les conversations textuelles. Cette évolution sera rendue possible grâce à GPT-5.6 Luna, qui devient le modèle par défaut pour les utilisateurs gratuits et les abonnés Go, en remplacement de GPT-5.5 Instant. Jusqu'à présent, les utilisateurs gratuits étaient limités à 10 messages toutes les cinq heures avant de basculer vers un modèle plus léger. Les abonnés Go, de leur côté, disposaient d'un quota de 160 messages toutes les trois heures. Ces restrictions disparaîtront désormais pour les échanges en texte. En revanche, les fonctionnalités plus gourmandes en ressources, comme l'analyse d'images, l'envoi de fichiers ou l'utilisation de certains outils intégrés, resteront soumises à des limitations. OpenAI précise également qu'elle pourra appliquer des restrictions ponctuelles afin de prévenir les usages abusifs. Les utilisateurs gratuits et Go bénéficieront aussi d'un nouveau mode baptisé « Réflexion », destiné aux questions les plus complexes. Lorsqu'il est activé, GPT-5.6 Luna prendra davantage de temps pour élaborer une réponse plus approfondie. Le modèle GPT-5.6 Sol, plus puissant, reste quant à lui réservé aux abonnés Plus et Pro. OpenAI indique avoir amélioré ses performances, avec des réponses plus précises, plus concises et comportant moins d'erreurs factuelles. Pour l'entreprise dirigée par Sam Altman, cette décision constitue « une étape concrète vers une intelligence plus accessible à tous ». Elle marque un changement de stratégie majeur, alors que, depuis le lancement de ChatGPT, les limitations d'utilisation constituaient l'un des principaux arguments pour inciter les utilisateurs à souscrire une offre payante. OpenAI, qui revendique désormais plus d'un milliard d'utilisateurs, n'a toutefois pas expliqué comment elle compte absorber le coût supplémentaire lié à la suppression des limites sur les conversations textuelles, alors que chaque requête adressée au chatbot représente une dépense en puissance de calcul. items.title: Blé, viande, bétail : les nouveaux droits d'importation publiés au Bulletin officiel
items.description: Le dernier numéro du Bulletin officiel a publié les détails du décret n° 2.26.583 relatif à la prolongation de la perception des droits d'importation sur le blé tendre et ses dérivés, ainsi que du décret n° 2.26.584 portant sur la suspension et la modification des droits d'importation applicables aux animaux domestiques vivants, à leurs viandes et à leurs abats. Voici les détails. Les deux décrets portent sur les mesures douanières adoptées par le gouvernement marocain concernant les importations de blé tendre et de produits d'origine animale. Pour rappel, les textes avaient été adoptés lors du Conseil de gouvernement du 22 juillet dernier. Concernant le décret n° 2.26.583, signé le 23 juillet 2026, il prolonge la perception des droits d'importation sur le blé tendre et ses dérivés, classés sous les positions tarifaires 1001.99.00.19 et 1001.99.00.90, pour la période allant du 1er au 31 août 2026. Une fois cette période passée, et à titre dérogatoire aux dispositions de la loi de finances n° 25.00, le texte du décret prévoit la suspension totale des droits d'importation à compter du 1er septembre 2026. Cette mesure s'inscrit dans la continuité du décret n° 2.26.419, publié en mai 2026, relatif au rétablissement puis à la suspension des droits d'importation sur le blé tendre et ses dérivés. Pour ce qui est du décret relatif aux produits d'origine animale, n° 2.26.584, le gouvernement a prévu la suspension des droits d'importation sur les ovins domestiques vivants, ainsi que sur les viandes de bovins, d'ovins, de caprins et de camélidés (positions tarifaires 0201, 0202, 0204 et 0208.60), jusqu'au 31 décembre 2026. Cette disposition ne concerne toutefois pas les abats de ces animaux destinés à l'abattage. En effet, le texte fixe le droit d'importation applicable aux abats de bovins, d'ovins, de caprins et de camélidés (position tarifaire 02.06 Ex) à 30 %, et ce jusqu'à la fin du mois de décembre 2026. A noter que l'exécution de ces deux décrets a été confiée au ministre délégué auprès de la ministre de l'Économie et des Finances, chargé du Budget et contresignés par le ministre le ministre de l'Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime, du Développement rural et des Eaux et Forêts, Ahmed El Bouari, ainsi que le ministre de l'Industrie et du Commerce, Ryad Mezzour. Ces mesures s'inscrivent dans la politique du gouvernement visant à garantir l'approvisionnement du marché national et à limiter la hausse des prix des produits alimentaires stratégiques, notamment en raison de la hausse de la demande et de la baisse du cheptel national après la sécheresse qui a frappé le pays. Les mesures visant l'importation de la viande rouge s'inscrivent aussi dans l'objectif de créer plus d'offre afin que les prix puissent reprendre leur cours normal après avoir fortement augmenté ces dernières années. En ce qui concerne le blé tendre, les mesures devraient permettre aux importateurs de constituer des stocks stratégiques pour une denrée essentielle à l'alimentation des Marocains. The post Blé, viande, bétail : les nouveaux droits d'importation publiés au Bulletin officiel appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: MAGA’s Most Famous Prisoner Is Free
items.description: E arlier this year, Tina Peters was languishing in a Colorado women’s prison, eating processed food, and complaining of declining health—including a persistent cough, digestive issues, and bumps on her skin. But by the end of June, the woman who was convicted on charges tied to tampering with voting equipment under her control in 2020 strolled into the White House, sporting a tailored pinstripe suit and red lipstick, her hair cut in a sharp bob. She feasted on a fried-chicken-and-noodle dish with President Trump in his private dining room and posed for photos in the Oval Office. She told the president about her ordeal and “what prison does to a person,” and they both bemoaned the state of the nation’s voting systems. “He was kind. He listened,” Peters told me in an email. Peters, once a martyr to the MAGA cause, is now a free woman, feted by the stolen-election movement. The former clerk and recorder of Mesa County, Colorado, was convicted in 2024 and sentenced to nearly nine years in prison after prosecutors said she deceived colleagues to grant an unauthorized person access to voting equipment. After returning to office, Trump, aided by his White House counsel and Justice Department, spearheaded a campaign to “Free Tina Peters” as MAGA commentators and her attorneys relentlessly used the power of their keyboards to demand her release. But because Peters was convicted of state charges, the only person with the power to get her out was Colorado Governor Jared Polis. The Democrat bowed to extraordinary pressure in May and granted Peters clemency despite pleas from prosecutors, his clemency board, and election officials that her punishment was just. Peters was released on June 1 after serving about 20 months of her sentence. Her freedom came as Trump ordered the nation’s intelligence community to find proof of foreign interference in the 2020 presidential election—only for it to again come up empty. That hasn’t stopped Peters, who wants the government to go even further in its efforts to find fraud she alleges exists from 2020 and overhaul rules and systems over the next three months to prevent malfeasance in November’s midterm elections . [ Read: Trump still hasn’t found what he’s looking for ] She walked out of prison repeating many of the unsubstantiated claims that helped land her behind bars. She immediately hit the MAGA circuit, appearing on podcasts and livestreams from locations that look straight out of Architectural Digest . She has crusaded against the machinery used to conduct American elections, insisting that votes have been flipped and that foreign adversaries could exploit future contests. She rails against prison conditions and calls for one of her critics—Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold, a Democrat—to be locked up. Her comeback tour has taken her around the country, including, on June 30, to the White House’s Presidential Walk of Fame, where a photo showed her glancing adoringly at Trump’s portrait while holding what appeared to be a Birkin bag. During the visit she and Trump talked about “election integrity,” Peters told me, including “why people need a process they can verify—paper, open counts, accountability.” Peters has said in nearly all of these media appearances that the actions that landed her in prison were an attempt to expose irregularities in her county’s voting equipment. She insists that her incarceration was “retribution” for showing that votes could be flipped—though there is no evidence of that claim. Ahead of the midterms she is imploring Trump to declare a national emergency on elections as a way to try to assert federal control over contests that are, by constitutional design, run by state and local governments. “We don’t have to prove anymore that these machines are cheating, that the ballots are being harvested,” Peters told War Room , a show hosted by the Trump ally Steve Bannon. The chyron identified her as a Former Political Prisoner. No longer subjected to rigid routines, head counts, or fixed mealtimes, Peters has enjoyed choosing her own food again, including steak, salads, and juicy tomatoes (“things that taste like they came from a kitchen instead of a tray.”) “Right now I’m trying to get healthy,” Peters told me. “See the people I love, and keep doing lawful work. I’m not interested in living bitter.” Her faith helped her endure especially tough moments. “I’m grateful to God,” she wrote. “Some days feel normal. Some don’t.” Peters must get permission from a parole officer before traveling out of state. Election denial has become her full-time job. She directs supporters to her recently revamped website, where she asks that they contribute to her cause (a red “Donate” button hovers in the top-right corner). At a “Fraud Fighter Summit” off the Las Vegas Strip in June, Peters took the stage, clutching a bouquet of flowers, to the delight of the crowd, and a moderator gushed about how “wonderful” she looked. Peters talked on speakerphone with Roseanne Barr, who had planned to attend the conference but had to scrap her trip. “Congratulations for being released from detainment in a communist country, Tina,” the sitcom star said. “You are our hero.” They pledged to take a girls’ trip at some point soon. Hawaii, Peters said, sounded like a good destination, adding: “I can still travel.” P eters has a history of finding herself embroiled in election disputes. She was elected Mesa County clerk and recorder in 2018 after campaigning on a promise to reopen a closed DMV office. Fruita, Colorado, got its motor-vehicles branch back, but Peters soon found herself in the middle of her first voting-related controversy. Nearly 600 ballots cast in a November 2019 election were found in a drop box outside the clerk’s office months later; an effort to recall Peters over the discovery failed to collect enough signatures. In November 2020 Trump won Mesa County, amassing nearly two-thirds of votes cast. But that election, Peters claimed in 2021, was tainted. Prosecutors said that Peters ordered video cameras to be turned off and deceived colleagues to obtain credentials that allowed an election-denial activist to access election equipment. Peters ran for Colorado secretary of state, despite being charged with numerous felonies, on a platform that included the claim that election equipment posed a threat to democracy. She lost in the primary. In 2024, a jury found her guilty of seven charges, including four felonies. The judge presiding over the case called Peters a “charlatan” and said that Peters, not faulty equipment, posed a threat to the electoral process. Trump returned to the Oval Office a few months after her conviction and quickly started a campaign to spring her from prison through pressure and threats of retaliation. He warned that “harsh measures” would ensue if she remained incarcerated and directed his Justice Department “to take all necessary action to help secure the release of this ‘hostage.’” Peters was convicted on state charges beyond Trump’s pardon power, but in December he issued one anyway. Senior U.S. District Court Judge R. Brooke Jackson, in a preliminary order blocking the administration’s threat to cut Colorado’s SNAP benefits, noted in March that Trump called Polis “weak and pathetic” for keeping Peters confined, and that the administration had launched “a barrage of threats and actions designed, by all appearances, to punish Colorado.” They included terminating millions of Department of Transportation funds, threatening cancellation of energy funds, announcing a plan to dismantle the Boulder-based National Center for Atmospheric Research , and denying federal disaster-relief assistance. An appeals court upheld Peters’s conviction a few weeks later, but found that the judge who presided over her case may have improperly considered her public comments—violating her First Amendment rights—and ordered that she be resentenced. Instead, Polis decided to commute her sentence. He wrote that hers was an “extremely unusual and lengthy sentence for a first time offender who committed nonviolent crimes.” An addendum to her clemency application that I obtained shows she acknowledges having “made mistakes,” that she pledged to obey the law if released, and that she noted that she wouldn’t have the ability to commit similar crimes since she is no longer a county clerk. “My work to ensure honest elections,” she wrote, “will continue.” W hen Peters was freed, on June 1, Francis McClelland was ready to greet her. Carrying a handmade sign reading Tina Peters Mahalo for Your Sacrifice Fight Fight Fight, the 69-year-old stood outside of the La Vista Correctional Facility in Pueblo with a handful of other supporters. McClelland had never understood why Peters would be imprisoned for trying to help prove that elections are rigged, and so he rented a car in Philadelphia and drove out to Colorado hoping to see her. But he made the trip in vain. Neither state-prison officials nor those close to her would say where she was, citing security concerns. “I just wanted to be in the area and if she saw the sign, just to know that, ‘Hey, man, you made a sacrifice,’” McClelland, an independent Trump supporter from Hawaii, told me. “You shouldn’t back down when you’re right,” he said. “I do believe she’s right.” [ Listen: The election deniers are in charge now ] Peters told me her early days outside of prison were mostly quiet, and devoted to the simple pleasures of her new freedom. She slept, and ate avocados. She went outside without asking permission. “I called people,” she told me. “I hugged people. I did boring grown-up stuff you can’t do inside. It wasn’t a parade. It was me trying to feel like a person.” In her first media appearance after her release, on War Room , Peters appeared alongside a friend and looked tired. “I feel like I’ve aged about 10 years,” she said. She called her release a “miracle” and thanked Trump, her attorneys, and the supporters who sent money through her website. She said she had a long road to clear her name and then went right back to the themes that had landed her in trouble, saying that Democrats “are going to cheat” in elections. “No one’s really addressing the problem that I spent my time in prison as retribution for,” she said. “And that was exposing the election machines that allow the votes to be flipped. As we’re coming up to our 250-year anniversary, I’m joyful that we still have our liberty but, at the same time, I’m very concerned and burdened with why no one is talking about this.” The Tina Peters tour hasn’t stopped since. She joins the MAGA-sphere from a constantly changing rotation of tastefully decorated settings, including a room with small duck figurines in the background and another with furniture upholstered in black-and-white chevron. She was spotted at a gathering with Arizona’s Kari Lake, another prominent voice in the election-skeptic movement. And wherever she appears, she always implores viewers to hit that red “Donate” button on her site. In June, a 12-hour online “Lift Tina Telethon” featured a roster of MAGA personalities applauding her sacrifice. She was likened to Joan of Arc and Nelson Mandela, and someone suggested that her face should be carved into Mount Rushmore. A banner crawling across the bottom of the screen asked viewers to Please DONATE NOW to reach a fundraising goal that one speaker set from $1 million to $2 million. Peters made her appearance midway through, and choked up almost immediately. She spoke of her time in prison, during which she wrote letters to Trump, and of a call she had with the president after her release. “I told him, ‘I only wrote two people while I was in prison,’” she said. “I got thousands and thousands of letters. I’m just so humbled and grateful because you guys were, and still are, the wind beneath my wings.” Peters said she told Trump she was discouraged that little progress had been made to secure election equipment. She hoped to talk more about it with him soon. She was staring down other problems, the kind that viewer donations might fix: Her air-conditioning had gone out, and so had the brakes on her truck. “It’s real difficult for me to ask for myself,” she said. The tour’s biggest stop, the White House, came at Trump’s request, according to Peters’s attorney Peter Ticktin. “He really admires her because she’s an American hero—and he referred to her as such,” Ticktin, a longtime friend of the president’s, told me. “She’s the one he wanted to meet.” Ticktin declined to say what was discussed. Peters said she felt valued during that visit. She spoke with the president about what she saw as a county clerk, how prison affects people, and of the need for “paper, open counts, accountability” in elections. “He talked like he actually cares what happens to regular people,” she wrote to me, “which is not how a lot of papers write him up.” At one point during the visit, she clutched a red AMERICA IS BACK! hat. She also met with Ed Martin, the U.S. pardon attorney, and was presented with a gold eagle brooch representing the Eagle Forum, the conservative advocacy group founded by Phyllis Schlafly. The White House spokesperson Abigail Jackson did not answer questions about the meeting with Peters, but said in a statement that “President Trump is committed to ensuring that Americans have full confidence in the administration of elections, and that includes totally accurate and up-to-date voter rolls free of errors and unlawfully registered non-citizen voters.” Trump wants Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship and voter ID to vote, as well as “other legislative proposals that would establish a uniform standard of photo ID for voting, prohibit no-excuse mail-in voting, and end the practice of ballot harvesting,” Jackson wrote. Two weeks after Peters visited the White House, Trump delivered a primetime address on election security, but again failed to provide clear evidence of fraud in the 2020 election. Many, including Peters, had hoped for more. On X, she called on Trump to “declare a National emergency” surrounding elections “to protect our country.” She later joined a handful of other election activists calling on federal officials to enforce a “Risk Mitigation Election Plan” before November that would, among other things, require hand-counting each ballot for federal contests before votes are certified, and compare them with counts tallied by electronic tabulators. “The objective is clear: reduce the opportunity for cheating,” read a July 24 letter from the activists to the acting director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. CISA did not answer my questions about the activists’ proposed plan or a meeting the activists said they had with the agency. Many of the people who administer America’s elections are dismayed by Peters’s post-prison celebrity. Her efforts to convince people that their elections can’t be trusted make the job of administrators more difficult and dangerous, they told me. “She didn’t learn a thing,” Carly Koppes, the Weld County, Colorado, clerk and recorder, said. “Her stance on ‘remorse’ is despicable, and she’s doing exactly what we told the governor she was going to do.” Tiffany Lee, the clerk and recorder from La Plata County, told me she and her staff cried with relief when Peters was sentenced. Now she is angry about what she termed Peters’s “sabotage” road show. "I knew for a fact that she would go right back to getting the attention," Lee said. When I asked Peters what she would say to people who allege that her claims are false, she deflected. “I didn’t create the mistrust,” she wrote in the email. “For years the public got told everything was the most secure ever, and basic questions got treated like a threat. Now a lot of Americans say they don’t trust the process.” Peters has her own ideas for making elections more secure. “Yelling at citizens won’t fix it. Proof will. Hand-marked paper. Paper poll books. Chain of custody. Counts people can watch, especially in federal races. That’s clearer than black-box machines and electronic poll books,” she wrote. “Making an election observable isn’t an attack on the country. It’s how you earn confidence back.” Election experts mostly dismiss these proposals as impractical, or warn they could produce large-scale errors. Peters’s podcaster pals, attorneys, and online supporters told me they see her as a symbol of a broader resistance against forces of evil who are attempting to overtake America. “She’s very brave,” Steve Stern, a Republican activist in Broward County, Florida who hosts The Stern American Show on Rumble, told me. (Peters has treated his audience to interviews at least twice since her release.) “She’s trying to do something to help the country.” Ticktin and another of her attorneys, John Case, told me they have earned no money from representing Peters. “Hopefully someday I’ll get fully compensated,” Case said, laughing. “But it’s doubtful. I’m not doing it for money—I’ll put it that way.” (At one point in his career, he charged $350 an hour.) Ticktin told me the work he’s doing at his own expense to help Peters is bigger than her: It’s about exposing “the biggest crime in the history of the United States—to steal our country.” Peters told me that some of her supporters were misled by fundraising pages that had nothing to do with her. Donations made on her website, she said, help pay for “legitimate costs: legal bills, security when needed,” and travel expenses for her advocacy work. Her saga damaged some of her relationships with family members, she said. “That still stings,” she wrote. “I’m very grateful for my mom, for the family who stayed, and for the friends and supporters who didn’t throw me away.” She said she is doing ordinary things with family members and catching up on the past two years. When I talked briefly on the phone with her last month, she said she was traveling. “I’ll be in Texas tomorrow; I’ll be in different places the next few days,” she told me, her voice carrying a hint of a southern drawl. She later stressed that she’s traveling for work, not play. When Peters first hit the election-activist circuit, the movement was dismissed by many elected officials and experts as “fringe.” Six years later, with Trump back in office and election deniers winning races up and down the ballot nationwide, the movement has been mainstreamed within the GOP even as the public’s trust in elections has declined. Their attempts to one day prove that 2020 was stolen may never bear fruit. But activists are already gearing up to uncover the fraud they believe might help Democrats win back Congress in 2026.

items.title: Odinkalu raises fresh questions on Tinubu’s academic records, nationality
items.description: Human rights lawyer and former National Human Rights Commission governing council chairman, Prof. Chidi Odinkalu, has questioned the publicly available information on President Bola Tinubu’s early education, parentage and nationality. Odinkalu raised the concerns during a recent interview with Nigeria Info FM, in remarks that have since resurfaced on social media. The lawyer questioned the availability of records relating to Tinubu’s primary and secondary education, as well as what he described as unanswered questions about the President’s background. He also questioned whether Tinubu may have received his early education at home, referring to a position he attributed to Minister of Foreign Affairs, Yusuf Tuggar, though he specifically named Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Festus Keyamo, in the interview. “But what if he was taught at home? And who now claims to have gone to university? If he was homeschooled as Festus Keyamo posited, famously, the Senior Advocate of Nigeria, then they should say so,” he said. Odinkalu argued that even if Tinubu had been homeschooled, there should ordinarily be some form of certification documenting his educational progression before university. “Homeschool is a preparatory process. After that you go forward for certification, right?” he asked. The human rights lawyer also referred to previous educational information allegedly attributed to Tinubu, questioning claims involving institutions such as Government College, Ibadan. He further questioned how a person could establish a university education without corresponding records of primary and secondary schooling. “Now they are trying to make up records or to clean up records in order to align with a current eligibility threshold. How do you not go through primary and secondary certification but you have a university degree?” he asked. Odinkalu also argued that the school attended by a future president should be regarded as significant, regardless of its location. “Is it not an achievement for a school to have produced a president? No matter how remote the school could have been,” he said. Drawing from his own experience, Odinkalu said he began his primary education as an internally displaced person following the Nigerian Civil War. “I started off primary school as an internally displaced person after the Nigerian Civil War. And I know the primary school I started off in, if I mention it to you, it’s not in any place on the map. But I take pride in it and I take pride in the fact that I passed through that primary school,” he said. The comments come amid renewed online discussions about Tinubu’s background and the records surrounding his early life. However, the claims made by Odinkalu during the interview remain his assertions and have not, in the material cited, been independently established. The post Odinkalu raises fresh questions on Tinubu’s academic records, nationality appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Guinée : Vers une grève à la BCRG…
items.description: La tension monte entre le syndicat et les autorités de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG). La Délégation syndicale de l’institution avec le Mouvement syndical de Guinée, a officiellement déposé un préavis de grève auprès du Gouverneur de la BCRG. Dans une correspondance datée du 6 août 2026, les représentants syndicaux notifient au Gouverneur leur décision d’engager une procédure de grève conformément aux dispositions des articles 431.3 et suivants du Code du travail. Le préavis doit prendre effet à compter du lundi 10 août 2026 et courir jusqu’au jeudi 20 août 2026, sauf prorogation ou levée anticipée décidée par le Bureau syndical. Mais les syndicats ne comptent pas en rester à cette période de préavis. Dans leur courrier, ils préviennent qu’à son terme, la Délégation syndicale pourrait déclencher une grève à durée indéterminée, jusqu’à la signature du protocole d’accord 2026. Le refus de signer le protocole d’accord au cœur du désaccord À l’origine de cette décision, les représentants syndicaux évoquent le refus du Gouverneur de signer le protocole d’accord 2026. Selon le document consulté par Guineenews, ce protocole découle des négociations menées avec le Cabinet de la BCRG autour de la plateforme revendicative 2026. Pour la partie syndicale, les discussions engagées doivent désormais aboutir à la formalisation de cet accord. C’est précisément l’absence de signature qui constitue, selon les syndicats, le principal motif du préavis. Les syndicats donnent encore une chance au dialogue Malgré cette menace de grève, la correspondance ne ferme pas la porte aux négociations. La Délégation syndicale demande au Cabinet du Gouverneur de prendre les dispositions nécessaires pour parvenir à une solution. Les syndicalistes disent ainsi vouloir éviter un durcissement du mouvement et appellent à une issue « favorable et constructive » au différend. Autrement dit, l’échéance du 20 août apparaît comme une période de dialogue supplémentaire. Si aucun compromis n’est trouvé d’ici là, la Délégation syndicale annonce qu'elle se réserve le droit de passer à une grève à durée indéterminée, jusqu’à la signature du protocole d’accord 2026. La correspondance est également adressée en copie à la FESABAG ainsi qu’à l’Inspection générale du Travail (IGT). Désormais, la balle est donc dans le camp de la direction de la BCRG, alors que s’ouvre une nouvelle séquence de négociations qui pourrait permettre d’éviter une paralysie prolongée de la première institution.

items.title: I wouldn’t be hurt if Afenyo-Markin’s ‘disrespectful’ comment was made privately – Nana Yaa Jantuah
items.description: Presidential Staffer Nana Yaa Akyenpim Jantuah has responded to Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin’s criticism over her role in receiving the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) petition, saying she would not have been offended if his comments had been made privately. Mr Afenyo-Markin had questioned the decision by the Presidency to assign Nana Yaa Jantuah to receive the petition following the NPP’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration, describing the move as disrespectful to the party. But speaking on Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen on Thursday, August 6, Nana Yaa Jantuah said the concern was not necessarily the description used against her, but the fact that it was made publicly in the presence of journalists and political actors. “If Afenyo-Markin had used ‘nobody’ remarks privately, I wouldn’t be angry. If he had told me this off air, I wouldn’t be hurt,” she said. She questioned why the Minority Leader chose to make the comment in front of media personnel covering the event. “Look at the number of media personnel on the ground and everywhere. What is he talking about?” she asked. Nana Yaa Jantuah said she has always shown respect to Mr Afenyo-Markin during their engagements and expected the same in return. “I give you a lot of respect when I see you, but you don’t want to give respect,” she stated. She further argued that the comments were not only directed at her but also questioned President John Dramani Mahama’s decision to nominate her as the government representative to receive the NPP’s petition. According to her, the focus should have remained on the issues raised in the petition rather than the individual assigned to receive it. Afenyo-Markin’s concerns During the presentation of the petition, the Minority Leader said the choice of Nana Yaa Jantuah as the recipient did not reflect the seriousness of the concerns raised by the opposition party. “With great respect to you and without prejudice to your presence, to nominate only you to come amounts to disrespecting us as a political party,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin pointed to the presence of senior NPP officials and parliamentary leaders at the demonstration, arguing that a higher-ranking government representative should have received the petition. “I’m the leader of the party in Parliament. You have the General Secretary of the party here. You have the Chief of Staff of the flagbearer. We have the Chairman of the Constitutional Affairs Committee of the party,” he stated. He added that members of Parliament and party leadership had participated in the demonstration and believed the government’s response should have reflected the significance of the issues being presented. “But to disrespect our democracy by only nominating you to come, like I said, with great deference to you, it doesn’t match it,” he said. The NPP staged the “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on Thursday, August 6, to present petitions to the Executive, Legislature and Judiciary over concerns including alleged selective justice, politically motivated arrests and threats to democratic governance. The Presidency has not announced any further action regarding the petition submitted by the opposition party.

items.title: UMaT commissions demonstrative underground mine to improve mining education and skills training
items.description: The University of Mines and Technology (UMaT) has commissioned a demonstrative underground mine to give students practical exposure to underground mining operations and strengthen skills development. The facility, constructed within the basement of the university’s administration block, is intended to serve as a practical training and research space for students and professionals in the mining-related disciplines. The initiative was started by the immediate past Vice Chancellor of UMaT, Professor Richard Amankwah, after identifying the potential of the largely unused basement space. Explaining the idea behind the project, Prof. Amankwah said the basement was originally designed for the storage of materials but was converted into a demonstrational mine to create opportunities for hands-on training. The facility is expected to allow students to experience features of an underground mine without having to leave the university campus. For Geomatic Engineering students, the facility provides an opportunity to undertake underground surveying, take points for mine planning and understand how underground locations relate to corresponding points on the surface. Mining students, meanwhile, can gain practical exposure to underground mine structures, including stopes and the handling of blasted material. The Chief Mine Inspector of the Minerals Commission, Joseph Frimpong, described the facility as a significant investment in the future of Ghana’s mining industry. He said the demonstration mine would serve as a “living laboratory”, enabling students to gain hands-on experience while bridging the gap between classroom theory and practical mining. Mr Frimpong also identified the facility as a potential hub for research and innovation, where students and researchers can develop solutions to emerging challenges in the mining sector. He urged students to view their education as an opportunity to contribute to national development, stressing that the skills acquired through the facility should help build industries that uplift communities, protect the environment and strengthen the country. The Minerals Commission official further called on UMaT to use the facility to support Ghana’s ambition of becoming a leader in sustainable mining while producing engineers who are globally competitive and committed to national development. The commissioning forms part of UMaT’s efforts to strengthen practical training and better prepare graduates for the demands of Ghana’s mining industry.

items.title: Guiriko : trois ministres encouragent les appelés à l’immersion patriotique à Bobo-Dioulasso
items.description: Guiriko : trois ministres encouragent les appelés à l’immersion patriotique à Bobo-Dioulasso Bobo-Dioulasso, 7 août 2026 (AIB) – Une délégation gouvernementale composée des ministres en charge de l’Enseignement de base, Jacques Sosthène Dingara, de l’Enseignement secondaire, Moumouni Zoungrana, et de l’Énergie, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, a rendu visite, vendredi, aux appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire au lycée mixte d’Accart-Ville de Bobo-Dioulasso. La délégation a pris part à la cérémonie de montée des couleurs nationales avant d’échanger avec les jeunes afin de les encourager à tirer pleinement profit de cette formation civique et patriotique. Le ministre en charge de l’Enseignement secondaire, Camarade Moumouni Zoungrana, s'est réjoui des premiers résultats observés sur les différents sites visités. « Nous voyons avec beaucoup de joie, en si peu de temps, le changement qui est en train de s'opérer. C'est la preuve du professionnalisme et du sérieux avec lesquels le travail est accompli », a-t-il déclaré, tout en remerciant les encadreurs. S'adressant aux appelés, il les a invités à cultiver le patriotisme, la dignité, le courage et la solidarité afin de contribuer au rayonnement du Burkina Faso. Selon lui, cette immersion permettra aux jeunes de mieux connaître leur pays, ses institutions et de réveiller les valeurs citoyennes qui sommeillent en eux. Il a exprimé le souhait de voir les participants devenir, à l'issue de la formation, des modèles au sein de leurs communautés. Pour le ministre en charge de l’Enseignement de base, camarade Jacques Sosthène Dingara, cette visite s'inscrit dans une mission confiée par le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré pour apporter le soutien du gouvernement aux appelés. Il a indiqué que cette immersion patriotique obligatoire prépare les futurs étudiants à une nouvelle étape de leur vie en développant le dépassement de soi, la camaraderie, l'unité, le civisme, l'amour de la patrie et le sens de la responsabilité. « Le gouvernement met tout en œuvre pour que cette formation contribue à faire de ces jeunes des leaders, des citoyens responsables et des patriotes pour les années à venir », a-t-il affirmé. À travers cette visite, la délégation gouvernementale a réaffirmé l'engagement des autorités à accompagner la réussite de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire, présentée comme un levier de renforcement des valeurs civiques et citoyennes chez la jeunesse burkinabè. Agence d'Information du Burkina CS/AB/wis

items.title: Santé : Le Burkina se dote d’une plateforme e-AGRÉMENT-MS pour simplifier les agréments des cliniques privées

Cette plateforme reçoit désormais les démandes d'agréments des cliniques privées. Fin des longues files d’attente pour les demandes d’agrément sanitaire. Elles se feront désormais en ligne au Burkina Faso grâce à la plateforme e-AGRÉMENT-MS. Ce portail en ligne est dédié à la gestion des demandes d’agrément, des conventions de partenariat, ainsi que des autorisations d’ouverture et d’exploitation des établissements sanitaires privés de soins. Il s’inscrit dans la dynamique de modernisation de l’administration publique engagée par le Gouvernement. Le ministre de la Santé Dr Robert Lucien Jean Claude Kargougou s’est dit « ému et fier » de cette avancée, qu’il qualifie d’étape majeure dans la transformation digitale des services publics de santé. Grâce à cet outil, les procédures d’agrément sont désormais dématérialisées, ce qui doit permettre d’accélérer le traitement des dossiers, de renforcer la transparence des processus et de faciliter l’accès des usagers à une information en temps réel. La plateforme est accessible à l’adresse suivante : https://e-agrement.minsante.bf. Minute.bf

items.title: Gold Fields Foundation supports Tarkwa Prison with 20-acre oil palm project for inmate rehabilitation
items.description: For Gold Fields Ghana Foundation Executive Secretary, Abdul-Razak Yakubu, prisons were once places he associated with fear. That perception, he says, began to change as he came to understand the Ghana Prisons Service not simply as an institution for keeping offenders in custody, but as a place where lives can be reformed and redirected. “Since that experience, whenever I see your uniforms, I get scared. But I am building the confidence to know that the prison is an institution for reformation,” he said. His remarks came as the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation launched the Prisons Agro-Support and Empowerment (PASE) Project at the Tarkwa Local Prison, supporting the cultivation of an additional 20 acres of oil palm. The initiative forms part of the Foundation’s broader investment in enterprise development and sustainable livelihoods in its host communities. The project seeks to use agriculture not only to supplement food production at the prison, but also to equip inmates with practical skills they can use after their release. The Tarkwa Prison already had 30 acres under oil palm cultivation. With a prison population of more than 340 inmates and a daily feeding allocation of only five Ghana cedis per inmate, prison authorities say expanding agricultural production is critical to supporting food needs while giving inmates productive opportunities. The Foundation has therefore provided 1,400 Tenera oil palm seedlings, fertiliser, organic compost, knapsack sprayers, weedicide, cutlasses and protective boots at a cost of about GH¢144,666 to establish the additional plantation. Commander of the Tarkwa Local Prison, Chief Superintendent Bright Gbogbo, says the project fits directly into the Ghana Prisons Service’s new strategic direction. He linked the initiative to the Director General’s “Think Ghana Prison Services” policy, particularly its focus on agricultural mechanisation, business and wealth creation, and strategic partnerships. According to him, agriculture offers inmates more than occupation while serving their sentences. It can provide them with vocational skills, self-reliance and opportunities for employment or entrepreneurship once they return to society. “The Ghana Prison Service is committed not only to the safe custody of inmates but also to their reformation, rehabilitation, and successful reintegration into society,” Chief Superintendent Gbogbo said. The prison authorities say the project is also expected to move beyond cultivation. The Gold Fields Ghana Foundation is considering the establishment of an oil palm processing centre, which would allow the prison to add value to its produce rather than depend entirely on external processors. Chief Superintendent Gbogbo disclosed that 1,400 seedlings had been supplied for the 20-acre plantation, with most already planted, while the Foundation is expected to support the prison with a processing machine. For Mr Yakubu, the ultimate measure of the intervention will not be the number of seedlings planted, but the lives changed. He said Gold Fields wants inmates leaving the prison to be able to point to the skills acquired during their incarceration as a foundation for a productive future. “We want people who leave your care to become the best agronomists and one day hold the microphone somewhere and say that I learned these skills when I was unfortunate or fortunate enough to be in the care of Ghana Prisons,” he said. The project is part of the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation’s stated commitment to creating value beyond mining, with investments in agriculture, livelihoods, skills development and community development. For the Tarkwa Prison, however, the ambition is broader than an oil palm plantation. It is about making rehabilitation practical giving inmates the skills, confidence and opportunity to build a different life when the prison gates eventually open.

items.title: Nana Yaa Jantuah to petition Speaker over Afenyo-Markin’s ‘disrespectful’ comment if he doesn’t retract
items.description: Presidential Staffer Nana Yaa Akyenpim Jantuah says she will petition the Speaker of Parliament if the Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, fails to retract his disrespectful comments directed at her. She said the comment was inappropriate and unacceptable, particularly because it was made publicly during the NPP’s presentation of its petition at the Jubilee House after its ‘Democracy Under Attack’ demonstration. Speaking on Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen on Thursday, August 6, Nana Yaa Jantuah questioned why Mr Afenyo-Markin would make such remarks about her while she was representing President John Mahama. “I’m going to petition the Speaker of Parliament if Afenyo-Markin does not retract… How can you tell me in front of everybody that I am a nobody?” She argued that the Minority Leader should have respected the authority of the President, who assigned her to receive the petition on behalf of the presidency. “He didn’t ask a security man. He didn’t ask a cleaner. The President nominated someone to come and receive your petition.” Nana Yaa Jantuah also defended her professional background, insisting that Mr Afenyo-Markin had no basis to diminish her contributions. “You don’t even know me. I give you a lot of respect when I see you, but you don’t want to give respect.” She said she remained silent at the time because she was representing the President and could not allow personal emotions to influence her conduct. “I didn’t open my mouth because I was standing there in the stead of the President of the Republic of Ghana.” She added that public officials should maintain respect in political engagements, particularly when interacting with women.

items.title: Jeux méditerranéens Tarente 2026 : 120 athlètes défendront les couleurs du Maroc
items.description: Le Comité national olympique marocain (CNOM) a dévoilé la composition de la délégation qui représentera le Royaume lors de la 20e édition des Jeux méditerranéens, prévue à Tarente (Italie) du 21 août au 3 septembre 2026. Au total, 120 athlètes, dont 72 hommes et 48 femmes, porteront les couleurs nationales dans 18 disciplines sportives, a indiqué le CNOM. La délégation marocaine a été officiellement enregistrée auprès du comité d'organisation de Tarente 2026, conformément aux listes proposées par les différentes Fédérations Royales Marocaines et aux critères de participation établis par le CNOM. Les représentants marocains seront engagés en athlétisme, boxe, escrime, football, gymnastique, haltérophilie, judo, karaté, lutte, natation, padel, sports de boules, sports équestres, taekwondo, tennis, tir sportif, triathlon et voile. Le football constitue la discipline la plus représentée avec 36 joueurs et joueuses, devant l'athlétisme (25 athlètes), la boxe (9), le karaté (7) et le taekwondo (6). Le Maroc alignera également cinq représentants en judo, tennis et lutte, tandis que les autres disciplines seront représentées par des athlètes qualifiés dans leurs spécialités respectives. À travers cette importante délégation, le Maroc ambitionne de réaliser une belle moisson de médailles et de confirmer sa place parmi les nations les plus compétitives des Jeux méditerranéens. items.title: Mali : le Premier ministre dresse le bilan des réformes et précise les priorités à venir du gouvernement
items.description: Le Premier ministre malien, Abdoulaye Maïga, a tenu un discours le 6 août a l'issue de la rencontre pour le bilan des cinq ans de la Transition au Mali, indiquant qu'un « cap important » avait ete franchi durant cette periode dans le processus de refondation et d'edification du Mali. Il a, dans ce contexte, indique que la finalite de ce travail collectif etait de mesurer « avec lucidite » le parcours du pays depuis le debut de la Transition, en ecoutant les preoccupations des Maliens et en fixant les priorites des prochaines etapes de l'action du gouvernement. Le cap devrait etre mis, selon le chef du gouvernement, sur le developpement de secteurs cles tels que l'industrialisation du pays, la transformation locale des matieres premieres, le developpement des infrastructures et l'amelioration des services sociaux. « Depuis cinq ans, notre pays s'est engage dans un processus de refondation visant a renforcer les fondements de l'etat, consolider l'autorite publique, restaurer la confiance entre les institutions et les citoyens, placer l'interet national au cœur de l'action publique », a declare Abdoulaye Maïga, citant, dans la foulee, les defis imposes par un contexte securitaire, economique et institutionnel difficile. Le secteur minier : un acquis majeur et levier de financement des projets du gouvernement La reforme du secteur minier figure parmi les changements majeurs lances par le gouvernement malien durant les cinq dernieres annees. « Grâce a la relecture du Code minier, a l'adoption de la loi sur le contenu local et a la renegociation des conventions minieres, les richesses du sous-sol malien profitent desormais davantage aux populations maliennes », a declare le Premier ministre, qui a aussi fait savoir que « plus de 760 milliards de francs CFA » (environ 1,33 milliard de dollars) avaient ete recouvres aupres des compagnies minieres operant sur le sol malien « au titre des redevances ajustees, des impots et du fonds minier de developpement ». Cette manne a permis « pour la premiere fois », selon Abdoulaye Maïga, de redistribuer « 18,4 milliards de francs CFA [plus de 32 millions de dollars] au benefice des communes du Mali pour financer des projets structurants en matiere d'eau, de sante, d'education et d'infrastructures de proximite ». Ces fonds sont devenus un levier de developpement territorial et de justice sociale, a-t-il affirme. Le gouvernement malien ambitionne de mettre a profit les ressources naturelles du pays, telles que l'extraction aurifere, pour transformer l'economie, creer des emplois et ameliorer les conditions de vie des populations maliennes, en bâtissant des ecoles, des centres de sante, des infrastructures energetiques et routieres et des opportunites d'emploi pour les jeunes. La Vision Mali Kura 2063 et SNEDD 2024-2033 : un « pacte de generations » pour bâtir un Mali souverain Le gouvernement malien prevoit d'accelerer la transformation structurelle de son economie, conformement a la Vision Mali Kura 2063 et a la Strategie nationale pour l'emergence et le Developpement durable, deux documents strategiques qui constituent un « pacte de generations » pour « bâtir un etat souverain, une economie competitive, une societe juste et un pays ou chaque citoyen pourra trouver les conditions de son epanouissement ». Le chef du gouvernement a fait etat des defis energetiques et securitaires qui s'imposent au pays et a appele a la responsabilite des Maliens pour y faire face. « Les cinq ans de la Transition auront permis de poser les fondations d'un Mali plus souverain, plus resilient et plus maître de son destin. Les defis demeurent, mais ils ne nous feront pas devier du cap », a-t-il promis.
